articleTitle: Image Classification Using Fuzzy Pooling in Convolutional Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Nowadays, deep learning models are increasingly required to be both interpretable and highly accurate. We present an approach that integrates Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) classification heads and Fuzzy Pooling into convolutional neural networks (CNNs). By utilizing the interpretability of KAN and the uncertainty handling capabilities of fuzzy logic, the integration shows potential for improved performance in image classification tasks. Our comparative analysis demonstrates that the modified CNN architecture with KAN and Fuzzy Pooling achieves comparable or higher accuracy than traditional models. The findings highlight the effectiveness of combining fuzzy logic and KAN to develop more interpretable and efficient deep learning models. Future work will aim to expand this approach across larger datasets.

articleTitle: Representative Item Summarization Prompting for LLM-based Sequential Recommendation
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Sequential recommendation aims to predict the next item based on historical behaviors. However, these sequential recommendation models are data-specific and require additional training to be applied to different datasets. To address this problem, recent studies have increasingly utilized Large Language Models (LLMs), known as their remarkable inference capabilities without additional training, to sequential recommendation task. Despite their success, there remain challenges to effectively utilizing LLMs for sequential recommendation. Previous LLM-based studies have employed In-Context Learning (ICL) to enable the LLMs to understand the input sequence and sequential recommendation task for generalized recommendations across various datasets without additional training. However, this approach is limited in the ability to capture user preferences from the semantic information of sequences due to a lack of user-specific information. To address this, we propose a prompt design strategy called RISP (Representative Item Summarization Prompting). Specifically, we select representative items by considering their similarity to the user's sequence. Then, we generate user preference information by summarizing these items through the LLMs. Finally, the user preference information is added to the prompt for the next item prediction, allowing the LLMs to make effective recommendations based on user preferences. We conduct experiments on three recommendation datasets and validate the effectiveness of our proposed method.

articleTitle: Harvesting Information Estimation Algorithm for Occluded Fruits in Autonomous Open-Field Orchard Robotic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In this study, we propose an efficient approach for recognizing harvesting information to perform grasping manipulation on fruits partially obscured by obstacles such as leaves and other fruits in an open-field orchard environment. Our method utilizes predefined 3D fruit models to more accurately reflect the true size of the fruits compared to traditional superellipsoid estimation methods. The proposed pipeline involves generating point clouds from 3D scans of real fruits, distinguishing fruit targets from obstacles using instance segmentation with the YOLOv8 model, and efficiently generating position and orientation information for grasping manipulation, even for partially occluded fruits.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Analysis of Neuronal Signal Streams: Estimating the Activity Range of Cultured Neuronal Networks in Consecutive Stimulus Inputs Using CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: We utilized a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) -that incorporates a structure designed to integrate local relationship features. The CNN-based deep learning approach enabled us to identify response patterns following stimulus input, using images of neural activity that depict the activity of individual neurons. The feature of CNN-based neural network, integrating local features, considered to contribute to decipher the relationship within time-series data, which are interpreted as streams of signals passing through a single neuron. Utilizing this feature, we attempted to determine the scope of activity that preserves the history of ongoing stimulation within a cultured living neuronal network. We repeatedly subjected the network to the same stimulus, and from the post-stimulus response activity, we extracted spatial combinations of neurons that fired simultaneously within brief 1 ms time windows. We calculated the firing rates for each of these 1 ms intervals in response to 10 different stimuli. By arranging these firing rates into a distinctive configuration that sustains temporal continuity, we generated images that illustrate neuronal activity. We then attempted to discriminate response images obtained at various stimulus intervals, and compared the accuracy of the discrimination to gauge the scope and degree of history retention in sequential activation.

articleTitle: Super Resolution of Remote Sensing Image Using Improved SwinIR
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In recent years, the number of satellite launches has been increasing. One of the reasons for this is the growing market for space development, which has led to the release of a large amount of satellite data. Among them are satellite images, which capture a wide range of ground conditions and are used in various fields, such as the extraction of building areas. However, human analysis of these images is time-consuming and inefficient, so deep learning is expected to be used for image analysis. The images that can be used to recognize objects in satellite images are high-resolution images taken by high-performance satellites, but such images are expensive, and the cost of acquiring a large number of images is high. In this paper, we propose a method to reconstruct a high-resolution satellite image by super-resolution from a low-resolution satellite image using the Vision Transformer model. Image Restoration Using Transformer (SwinIR) is adopted as the base model. To improve the accuracy, Knowledge Distillation and Multi-Layer Perceptron with Gating Unit are incorporated into the base model, and good results are obtained.

articleTitle: Empirical Research on 3D Analysis and Flow Prediction of Upstream Rivers Using Drones
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This study aims to develop an AI prediction system for watersheds, utilizing data from Sri Lanka and Vietnam in collaboration with overseas researchers. Initially, a foundational AI prediction system will be constructed, and basic data will be gathered based on river data from Japan. Subsequently, topographic data of the watershed area, managed by the joint research partner institution, will be incorporated into the AI prediction system through drone-based aerial measurement and analysis. Moreover, visits to the joint research institution will be conducted to gather information on water damage and electricity supply. This information will then be integrated into the AI prediction system. Utilizing the collected data and additional observation data, efforts will be made to enhance the accuracy of the AI prediction algorithm, identify potential issues, and overcome them. The ultimate goal is to establish new AI pre-diction technology by comparing the results of this study with both domestic and international research outcomes. This paper will present data from a drone scan of the upstream watershed and discuss the future use of AI based on the results of three-dimensional analysis and image processing.

articleTitle: Exercise Support System with Self-Growing Avatars Using Interactive Evolutionary Computation
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Continuous exercise is crucial for achieving health and physique goals, yet maintaining motivation can be difficult when physical results take time to become visible. In this paper, we propose a novel exercise support system leveraging interactive evolutionary computation (IEC) to generate self-evolving avatars personalized to users' ideal body shapes. The system employs motion capture technology to synchronize users' exercise movements with avatars that undergo progressive evolution towards their desired physical ideal based on IEC feedback. An experimental evaluation of the system revealed 81.8 % of participants reported heightened motivation to continue exercising after interacting with the self-evolving avatars. These results suggest that providing an embodied visualization of potential long-term outcomes could offer a compelling incentive to maintain exercise routines.

articleTitle: Passing Practice Support for Soccer Players Using First-Person Videos
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: We propose a novel visualization system to enhance soccer passing practice by providing potential pass courses and their scores. The proposed system is based on a first-person video footage captured during soccer play and extracts frames for pass-course suggestions using the rate of ground-surface pixels in the frame and depth estimation. Possible pass courses were scored according to their direction and distance to the closest player. To validate the proposed method's effectiveness, we conducted a series of experiments involving 17 participants, comprising 12 museum visitors and five university students. The estimated score of visualized pass courses using the proposed method was generally successful, whereas some pass courses received lower scores from participants owing to limitations in the system's ability to accurately detect the color of players' uniforms, which affected the overall evaluation of certain passing options.

articleTitle: Whole Time-Series Clustering by Embedding Relational Graphs into Vector Spaces Using DeepWalk
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Clustering is a type of unsupervised learning, which can be broadly classified into static and dynamic methods. Whole time-series clustering, one of the dynamic methods, is performed on multiple time-series data and classifies them. However, few whole time-series clustering methods take into account the fact that the clusters belonging to each time-series data change with time. Therefore, the purpose of this study is to propose a method to adapt static clustering methods to whole time-series clustering that takes into account the time variation of cluster classification. Specifically, we propose a method to perform static clustering for each time point of time-series data, embed a relationship graph consisting of clusters at each time point into a vector space, and perform time-series clustering by analyzing relationships among clusters at different time points. For embedding the graph into the vector space, we use DeepWalk, a method based on random walk. Numerical experiments are then conducted to verify the behavior of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Optimization Performance Analysis of Different Initialization Methods in Single-Objective and Multi-Objective Chaotic Evolution
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Chaotic Evolution (CE) is a significantly faster and more robust method for solving single-objective and multi-objective optimization problems. However, there are various factors that can impact the performance of CE, with population initialization being one of them. A well-executed initialization method can contribute to the discovery of better solutions and enhance both convergence rate and accuracy. This paper conducts a comparative experiment on CE algorithms using six different initialization methods. The performance of the CE algorithms utilizing these various initialization methods is analyzed and discussed. To assess convergence rate and accuracy, eight single-objective optimization benchmark functions and five multi-objective optimization benchmark functions are employed in our analysis. The evaluation results reveal significant disparities among the six initialization methods, indicating that different approaches to initialization have a substantial influence on the optimization performance of the CE algorithm.

articleTitle: Development of a Model for Discriminating Electroencephalograms of Patients with Mild Cognitive Impairment and Healthy Individuals Using a Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: We performed machine learning using spectrum analysis and power spectra of electroencephalograms (EEGs) of patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI). Spectrum analysis was performed on the EEGs of MCI patients and healthy individuals, and the power spectrum values of the two groups were calculated and compared. Based on the power spectrum values of the theta and alpha bands, models for discriminating MCI patients were created using a support vector machine (SVM), and their accuracies were compared. In the spectrum analysis, the theta band showed significantly higher power spectrum values in the MCI group. In the comparison of the accuracies of SVM models, the model using the theta band showed higher values in parameters, such as accuracy rate. These results suggested that the power spectrum values of the theta band are useful for discriminating MCI patients.

articleTitle: On Two Variants of Fuzzy Clustering for Relational Data
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In this paper, two fuzzy clustering algorithms are proposed for relational data. The first algorithm is obtained by regularizing a conventional algorithm for relational data, which is similar to how the Yang's penalized Fuzzy c-means can be regarded as regularizing the Bezdek's Fuzzy c-means. The second algorithm is obtained using the following two steps: First, separating the fuzzification parameter for membership and the cluster size controller in a conventional algorithm for relational data, second, regularizing the Tsallis-entropy. This procedure is similar to that a conventional algorithm for vectorial data can be regarded as separating the fuzzification parameter for the membership and that for the cluster size controller in that for another conventional algorithm and then regularizing the Tsallis-entropy. The features of our proposed algorithms are observed through numerical experiments using an artificial dataset.

articleTitle: Semantics Indoor Navigation Using a Path Finding and Spatial Mapping for Assisting Visually Impaired Person
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Visually impaired individuals face significant challenges when navigating unfamiliar indoor environments. Due to the complexity of indoor navigation, existing aids for the visually impaired, such as guide dogs and white canes, provide limited assistance in complex indoor settings. In this paper, we present an innovative approach to generating paths for indoor navigation for the visually impaired, utilizing JSON data based on floorplans combined with conventional pathfinding algorithms. Experimental results demonstrate the system's effectiveness in various indoor settings, highlighting its potential as a valuable tool for visually impaired individuals.

articleTitle: Estimating Shape and Size of Objects based on Exparts' Visual Perception
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: The highly sophisticated visual perception of experts provides inspection functionality for target objects such as engineering products, agricultural crops, affected areas in medical fields, constructions, and many others. They can intentionally and automatically switch their perceptual attention between global entirety and local precision using ambient and central vision. The developed method is designed to replicate this functionality in agricultural applications, identifying the shapes and sizes of plant leaves to estimate growth status. Experimental results showed that the performance of this method is almost equivalent to that of human experts.

articleTitle: Registration Method for Head CT and MR Images Based on TransMorph Incorporated ASPP
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In recent years, with the development of diagnostic imaging equipment, image fusion, which fuses medical images from multiple modalities, has been proposed as a diagnostic imaging application. This has the advantage of integrating images with different characteristics and resolutions into a single composite image, which compensates for the missing information of each and facilitates the reading of lesions. Examples of the use of fusion images include surgical simulation and CyberKnife-based surgery. To create a fusion image, the two images must be aligned. Currently, this is often done manually, which increases the burden on the surgeon and introduces problems such as variations in accuracy depending on the surgeon's skill. Therefore, this paper describes the development of an automatic registration method for creating a fusion image between head CT and MRI, which is necessary for CyberKnife-based surgery of brain tumors. The method uses TransMorph, a registration model, as the base model, and a new model is constructed by adding ECAM and ASPP. As a result, the proposed method with the introduction of ASPP to the base model shows an improvement in the mutual information value and succeeds in improving the accuracy.

articleTitle: Swin Transformer-Based Poisonous Mushroom Classification Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Mushrooms, which have long been used in various fields, were categorized using the Swin Transformer. Swin transformer is an improved model from the previous version, Vit. About 5000 images were used and 16 classes were categorized. If you add more images and classes later, it may become a basic model for developing a mushroom classification app.

articleTitle: Detection of Temporal Changes from Satellite Images Based on Improved SNUNet-CD
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Change Detection (CD) technology is an integral part of Earth observation in remote sensing (RS) image analysis. It is widely used in areas such as natural disasters, urban development monitoring, land resource management, and surveillance. As a pixel-to-pixel prediction task, the CD technique is location sensitive and requires more attention to feature extraction. Recently, deep learning (DL)-based CD methods have made various efforts to extract deep semantic features, but they ignore the importance of shallow layer information, including high-resolution and fine-grained features, which leads to uncertainty in the change-ground entities. To address these problems, SNUNet-CD is a model that mitigates the loss of localization information in the deeper layers and improves detection accuracy by using dense connections. Although it shows higher detection accuracy than other methods and provides a good trade-off between accuracy and computational complexity, it has difficulty in exploiting the different semantic and detailed information contained in deep and shallow features, which often blurs the target boundaries of the identified changes. Therefore, in this paper, we propose a model that incorporates Attention Gates, an attention mechanism that selectively highlights and updates salient regions of the feature map, into the skip-connection part to effectively link features of different levels. The performance evaluation results showed that Precision=0.9073, Recall=0.9127, and Fl-score=0.9099, confirming the effectiveness of introducing Attention Gates.

articleTitle: Evaluation of a Writing Skill Enhancement System Through Dialogue for Children with Developmental Disorders Using Companion Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: We have developed a writing skill enhancement sys-tem through dialogue for children with developmental disorders and investigated the impact of the presence or absence of a companion robot and differences in input methods. Some children with developmental disorders struggle with sentence writing skill. Although previous research has discovered the effectiveness of a robot intervention in social skill training for children with developmental disorders, few studies have conducted writing skill training for them and demonstrated its effectiveness. In this study, we aim to investigate four types of writing skill enhancement systems through dialogue with presence/absence of a companion robot and input methods (speech recognition/typing) for the effectiveness of improving the writing skills of children with developmental disorders. The dialogue system uses Chat-GPT, ChatAPIs, to generate responses. This paper investigated the four developed writing skill enhancement systems targeted at university students as a preliminary experiment for testing with children with developmental disorders. Experimental results showed a tendency to elicit a large number of words from the students through the interaction with the system using speech recognition and a companion robot. In addition, there was no consistent trend between the survey results and the system that was found to be most suitable, indicating the possibility of not being able to select an effective system based only on survey results.

articleTitle: An IEC-Driven Optimization of Gestures to Enhance Personality Traits in Communication Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In this study, we propose a system that optimizes the gestures used to express the personality traits of a communication robot according to user preferences. In order for a communication robot to make people feel comfortable, it is necessary to convey a friendly impression. However, conventional robot personalities are designed based on general human impressions and do not take individual users' preferences into account. In order to tackle this challenge, we present a system that utilizes Interactive Evolutionary Computation (IEC) to optimize the gestures employed to convey the personality traits of the robot, aligning them with the user's specific preferences. The effectiveness of the system was then verified through an experimental evaluation. As a result, it was suggested that the proposed method could help the robot convey better impression to users, thereby improving its familiarity.

articleTitle: On Variants of Fuzzy Clustering Algorithms with Dimension Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Two variants of the fuzzy c-means (FCM) clustering algorithm are focused in this work- Yang's FCM (YFCM) and the extended q-divergence-based FCM (EQFCM). These procedures of fuzzification have not been utilized in conjunction with dimension reduction methods to construct fuzzy clustering algorithms in existing literature. In this study, ten fuzzy clustering algorithms are considered by com-bining two procedures of fuzzification-Yang-type and ex-tended q-divergence regularization-and five dimension reduction methods-principal component analysis (PCA), probabilistic PCA (PPCA), t-distribution-based PPCA (t-PPCA), factor anal-ysis (FA), and t-distribution-based FA (t-FA). Numerical experi-ments conducted on one artificial dataset and two real datasets demonstrate that the combination of extended q-divergence regularization and t- FA outperforms all other combinations, as well as conventional methods, in terms of clustering accuracy.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Virtual Mock Interview Development
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into educational technologies marks a significant shift in learning methodologies and operational dynamics within educational institutions. At the forefront is an AI-driven virtual mock interview platform designed to address the high Customer Acquisition Costs (CAC) in the edtech sector, especially for interview preparation services. This initiative harnesses a blend of AI technologies, including ADA 2 for creating context-aware embeddings and Machine Learning (ML), to transform the traditional mock interview process into a dynamic, cost-effective system. Central to the platform is its use of advanced Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques and GPT-4 Large Language Model (LLM), automating the process of mock interviews and providing personalized feedback, ensuring a preparation journey that meets specific candidate needs and mirrors real interview scenarios. A key evaluation among 100 students from a cohort of 1800 demonstrated a 90% cost reduction for three mock interviews, reducing expenses from ₹3000 to just ₹300 per candidate. This cost efficiency significantly enhances access to quality interview preparation, improving student satisfaction and accessibility. Moreover, the platform provides valuable insights into student performance, setting a new standard in educational technology by offering an effective, personalized interview preparation experience. This project reflects a holistic approach to student development and the critical role of technology in addressing the evolving needs of learners

articleTitle: Assigning Transportation Modes to Workers Using Statistics in Japanese Synthetic Populations
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In this paper, we modify the precedent method to assign commuting option to each worker in synthetic populations. Synthetic population is a data with household compositions in a specific community. Based on the relations between residential place and workplace, we try to assign commuting options such as train, bus, automobile, motorcycle, bicycle and walk. Since the previous method considered only trains as commuting option using the ratio of workers who commute their working place by train, we include the ratio of workers who commute by their automobiles in this paper. Using publicly released statistics about commuting options in each city, we successfully assign appropriate commuting options to each worker.

articleTitle: Loss Balancing for Physics-Informed Neural Networks Considering Procedure for Solving Partial Differential Equations
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: With the development of machine learning, numerical analysis using neural networks has been devised. Remarkably, physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) enable physically consistent numerical analysis by introducing a loss function that conforms to relevant governing equations. Moreover, research is rapidly advancing for the application of PINNs to inverse analysis in areas such as physical property identification. For a PINN to learn governing equations, the weights of the loss functions should be properly determined because they have different roles in components such as boundary conditions, initial conditions, and governing equations. However, weight setting is generally challenging. We propose a loss balancing method considering the procedure for solving partial differential equations. The proposed method is validated through comparisons with conventional solvers.

articleTitle: Detection of Overhanging and Dead Branches from In-Vehicle Camera Images Using Deep Learning and Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In recent years, the construction industry has been promoting ICT (Information and Communication Technology) to address the decline in construction workers and improve working conditions. However, despite advancements in technology, the industry still relies on the visual inspections of skilled technicians, leading to enormous time and cost expenditures for the maintenance of social infrastructure and surrounding obstacles. In light of this situation, there is a growing demand for the development of inspection systems using deep learning. This study focuses on constructing an inspection system that targets dead branches on roadside trees in mountainous areas. In these areas, after typhoons, dead branches often get caught in roadside trees, posing a risk of falling. Therefore, it is necessary to check and remove them in advance. Since it is difficult to observe roadside trees while driving, the goal of this study is to improve the current situation by developing a system that can detect overhanging branches and dead branches caught in them.

articleTitle: Development of a Gesture Analysis System for Human System Interaction
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Recently, Japan has been facing various social issues, and to solve these problems, it is necessary to create a society where diverse people can live comfortably. To build such a society, appropriate support tailored to individuals is required, necessitating the analysis of various types of information to understand the people's needs at any given moment. In particular, analyzing non-verbal elements such as posture, facial expressions, and gestures is crucial, as these naturally indicate a person's condition. Therefore, this study focuses on human gestures, one of the non-verbal elements, and proposes a gesture recognition method using Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) and K-Means. We demonstrated that symbolic gesture recognition is possible by recording arm trajectories from skeletal measurements with an RGB-D camera.

articleTitle: Implementation of Pneumoconiosis Detection xAI in Chest X-ray Images
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This study aims to visualize pneumoconiosis lesions from chest X-ray images using an improved Grad-CAM method and evaluate its performance. Pneumoconiosis is a disease that causes fibrotic changes in the lungs due to the inhalation of dust, and there is no cure. Diagnosis is usually performed by interpreting chest X-ray images, which requires skilled radiologists who are in short supply. Recently, diagnostic support using deep learning has garnered attention, and visualization methods such as Grad-CAM are used to explain these supports. However, these methods have not been sufficiently validated and have issues such as low-resolution visualizations. We constructed a pneumoconiosis detection model using the VGG16 model and applied GradCAM, GradCAM++, ScoreCAM, and LayerCAM methods to visualize the lesions. The VGG16 model showed high performance with both sensitivity and specificity of 0.94 in detecting pneumoconiosis. While all visualization methods exhibited high specificity, sensitivity was generally low, with LayerCAM being the lowest. Although ScoreCAM showed potential usefulness, overall visualization performance was low. It was suggested that LayerCAM is unsuitable for diffuse lung diseases like pneumoconiosis. Additionally, the sensitivity might have decreased due to narrowing down the Activation Map values to 0.7 or higher. Future research requires precise annotation and expansion of datasets. The study indicated the usefulness of ScoreCAM as a method for detecting and visualizing pneumoconiosis from chest X-ray images, although improvements in overall visualization performance are needed. LayerCAM may not be suitable for visualizing pneumoconiosis.

articleTitle: Motion Simulation for Fatigue Reduction and Actual Measurement Using EMG
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Muscle fatigue is an important phenomenon in exercise. Muscle fatigue affects the duration of an activity, so delaying muscle fatigue can lengthen the duration of exercise. Furthermore, Muscle fatigue is one of the risk factors for musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs). Repetitive tasks, in particular, have been identified as a primary risk factor for MSDs. Force application with less muscle fatigue is essential for maintaining and improving exercise performance and preventing disease. In this study, we focus on generating movements that cause less muscle fatigue. The purpose of this study is to identify force application with less muscle fatigue and to actually measure these movements. Simulation and actual measurement will be conducted for the “back-and-forth rubbing motion with the arm”. The “back-and-forth rubbing motion with the arm” was set as one of the repetitive movements. Based on the simulation results, we will verify whether fatigue can actually be suppressed by actual measurement.

articleTitle: Generation of Natural Language Responses to Questions about the Relationship between Two Time-series Data
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: We propose a method for generating response sentences to questions about the behavior of two time-series data. For this task, it is necessary to analyze the behavior and the relationship of the data to generate sentences. For this purpose, we proposed a model that extends Transformer to capture the relationships among time-series data. We created a synthetic dataset and trained it to generate answers to questions about two time-series data. The explanatory targets for the time-series data are trends, period, degree of change, and temporal order relationships. We also created several different datasets that capture features of time-series data, and confirmed that the accuracy can be improved by learning the data step by step, starting from the basic features.

articleTitle: Inspection of Concrete Hollow Slabs Based on Object Detection in Electromagnetic Radar Received Images
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This study aims to improve the inspection efficiency of concrete hollow slab bridges by using electromagnetic radar-received images to detect insufficient cover thickness and sedimentation areas. By utilizing the object detection algorithm You Only Look Once (YOLO) and using Python scripts for data filtering and analysis, an efficient non-destructive anomaly detection system was constructed. This system significantly reduces time and costs compared to traditional visual inspections.

articleTitle: Image Recognition Imitating Saccadic Eye Movement in Grid Cell Net
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This paper proposes an autonomous focal location transition method that imitates saccadic eye movement for image recognition. Grid Cell Net (GCN) is an image recognition algorithm inspired by the human neocortex. GCN focuses on a part of the target image at the same time and sequentially changes the focal location on the target image. At each time step, GCN receives feature data from the focal location of the target image and the focal location transition. GCN recognizes the image from these time series data. However, the conventional GCN randomly transitions the focal locations to recognize the target image and lacks a mechanism to autonomously determine the focal location transition. The proposed method introduces an autonomic focal location transition to enhance image recognition by incorporating a candidate class selection and a next focal location prediction. The candidate class selection finds a promising recognition class at each transition step, while the next focal location prediction finds the next focal location that effectively reduces the recog-nition class candidates. Experimental results using the MNIST dataset show that the proposed method not only autonomously transitions the focal location but also achieves higher recognition accuracy compared to the conventional GCN.

articleTitle: Recognition Accuracy of the Vehicle Posture and the Operator's Face Posture When Operating a Small Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This paper investigated how accurately the operator of a boarding vehicle recognizes and operates the posture of the vehicle. We also compared the operation of a vehicle that can move in all directions (3DoF (degree of freedom)) with that of a vehicle that can move in 2DoF. An experimental system was constructed in which the operator boarded a vehicle in a virtual space and played a game in which he operated it to match its posture to a target. As a result of the operation, the situation in which the operator judged that the posture of the operation object matched that of the target was discussed. There was an error of approximately 10 degrees in the posture of the operation object and the target. The main cause of this error was the accuracy of the neck's sense of direction (the accuracy of recognizing the difference between the direction in which the operator's face is facing and the forward direction of the body). The results suggested that the accuracy of the neck orientation sense is lower when the operator is riding on a vehicle and operating it, compared to the stationary state. 3DoF operation of the vehicle was less accurate in posture operation than the 2DoF operation. The direction in which the operator's face was facing tended to be shifted in a clockwise direction from the forward direction of the operator's body.

articleTitle: Mixed-Reality Simulator for Analysis of Interactions between Humans and Crawler Cranes
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Crawler cranes are used in various applications, including plant construction and civil engineering. However, accidents caused by hazardous events, such as overturning the entire body or overshadowing of a suspended load, can be problematic. Because crawler cranes are large and powerful machines, simulators are required to analyze the relationship between such hazardous events and human operations. This study proposed a framework for a mixed-reality simulator to analyze the interactions between humans and crawler cranes. This framework combined the high-performance graphics capabilities of Unreal Engine 5 with the high-precision multibody dynamics analysis of MATLAB Simscape to create a visually and physically realistic simulation. Moreover, the quantification of the decision-making process was possible based on the eye-tracking information of the operator. This study described the implementation of these features and discussed the prospects for human-crawler crane interaction analysis using this simulator.

articleTitle: Estimation of Water Quality Status of Lake Hachiroko, Japan, Using Remote Sensing Data and Water Depth and Temperature
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This study investigated the effectiveness of a method using a neural network coupled with remote sensing, water depth, and temperature data in estimating water quality for multiple water quality parameters. The proposed method improved the accuracy of water quality parameter estimation, namely that of biochemical oxygen demand estimation, by 2.8 mg/L compared with the conventional method of fuzzy regression analysis.

articleTitle: Method to Develop Models of Natural Reasoning in Fuzzy Rule Evaluation Task
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Multiple studies in various areas have shown that human reasoning does not always parallel formal logic. Fuzzy Logic was formulated in part to tackle some of the differences, yet it alone does not fully elucidate several commonly observed patterns of human reasoning. LLMs and other advanced language models have shown patterns of human-like reasoning, as well as some differences from formal reasoning, when data from human communication is used to develop these models. This research aims to develop a method for modelling how people infer the validity of a given rule or statement, based on evaluation of a given set of fuzzy samples, in order to build models that can accommodate various inference methods observed in human reasoning. Experiments inspired by the Wason selection task logic puzzle are conducted to understand how people evaluate the validity of a rule for a given set of card samples. Analysis of the results of these evaluations shows that a small category fuzzy models account for much of the variation in responses from these experiments. These results suggest that conventional fuzzy and multi-valued inference methods are effective foundations for building and testing such systems and that they also require modifications to account for certain aspects of human reasoning as recorded in these experiments. Such explicitly defined rule-based systems, when they are able to accommodate human-like reasoning, may develop as effective foils for complex models that tend to be opaque and yet often suffer from similar issues due to the data used to train them.

articleTitle: A Study of Emotion-based Music Generation using Diffusion Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This research aims to develop a method that can generate a variety of music using a diffusion model, taking emotion as input and controlling it by musical attributes corre-sponding to the emotion as an approach to music generation. The diffusion model uses a method called Diffusion Language Model, which can control the generation of music by using a classifier at each time denoising stage, and the classifier identifies emotions using musical attribute values. Experiments were conducted to compare the music generated when the learning method and classifier were changed for the proposed method, and to evaluate whether the music reflected emotion or not. The results of the experiment did not confirm that music was generated for the input emotion, but did confirm that the characteristics of the generated music could be controlled by devising the learning method and classifier processing.

articleTitle: Pseudo-Holographic Display of Plant Models based on Pepper's Ghost Illusion
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: We propose a new display method for visualizing flower models using a pseudo-holographic technique known as the Pepper's ghost illusion. This classic optical illusion technique creates the appearance of floating objects by reflecting them off a transparent panel, thereby producing a convincing visual effect that simulates three-dimensionality. In our approach, we utilized this illusion to display six distinct flower models obtained from a comprehensive photogrammetry archive of various plant species. These models were rendered to overlay onto a transparent glass vase, enhancing the realism of quality. To facilitate user interaction with the displayed models, we incorporated a depth sensor (Intel D415) to track the user's hand position. A user study revealed that participants were notably attracted to the display, indicating successful capture of their attention. Feedback, however, suggested that the system requires enhancements in usability and depth perception to improve the overall user experience. Our future work includes addressing these limitations by developing a larger display setup that could accommodate more complex interactions and by integrating motion-parallax techniques to enhance the three-dimensional view. This could be implemented using head-tracking technology, further advancing the effectiveness of the pseudo-holographic display.

articleTitle: Development of a Robust Fuzzy $c$-Means Method Through Convex Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: The method of c-means and its extension, fuzzy c-means, obtain clusters by minimizing the sum of the squared distances between the data points and their nearest cluster centers. We apply the logarithm to the squared distance in order to improve the robustness of fuzzy c-means for outliers. We develop a clustering algorithm by reformulating the fuzzy c-means optimization problem as the minimization of a concave function and applying the convex-concave procedure. As a result of convex analysis techniques, we can easily prove the convergence of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Estimation of the Degrees of Tilt of the Upper Body Postural Body Axis Using Optical Motion Analyzer
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In recent years, the number of hemiplegia patients due to stroke has been increasing. Scaling for Contraversive Pushing (SCP) is a method to evaluate the severity of the stroke. In this evaluation method, it is important to quantify the body axis tilt numerically. In this study, we measured and analyzed the Side Tilt Angle of the upper body posture using an optical motion analyzer, and aimed to visualize the severity of postural localization disorder caused by body axis tilt. First, an angular accuracy experiment I was conducted for a parameter indicating Side Tilt Angel that was set. Then, an experiment II was conducted to compare the posture of a normal subject with eyes open and eyes closed. The error of Side Tilt Angle accuracy was within ±5.0 [degrees], and the standard deviation was within ±1.0 [degrees]. The results of the comparison experiment showed that no changes occurred between open and closed eye postures for the healthy subjects. In addition, a program was developed to separate the coordinates that were switched when two persons were captured, enabling the system to separate them. The development of this system is expected to increase the effectiveness of rehabilitation for hemiplegia.

articleTitle: ESWL Outcome Prediction with SMOTE and Stratified Sampling
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In recent years, extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy (ESWL) and transurethral lithotripsy (TUL) have become the primary treatments for ureteral stones. ESWL is less physically burdensome than TUL and requires a shorter treatment period, but its success rate is lower compared to TUL. Therefore, selecting the appropriate treatment method in clinical practice is essential. This study aims to reduce the physical and financial burden on patients by predicting the outcomes of ESWL, thereby minimizing the need for dual treatments. In this study, stratified sampling was performed on the features examined in previous studies and combined with oversampling by SMOTE to assess the impact on the prediction accuracy of ESWL outcomes. As a result, we confirmed that stratified sampling and SMOTE improved prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Improving the Learning Efficiency of Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning SUHRL Using Transition Information Between Subgoals
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: The hierarchical reinforcement learning approach incorporates intrinsic motivation into reinforcement learning. In this approach, the agents are hierarchically organized into a higher-level strategy that learns the application order (plan) of sub goals and a lower-level strategy that learns the sequence of actions up to the subgoals. This incorporation has been shown to facilitate problem-solving even in environments with sparse rewards. Stepwise Unified Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (SUHRL) has been proposed as a hierarchical reinforcement learning algorithm. SUHRL enables autonomous learning without the need for prior knowledge or predefined subgoals. However, learning efficiency is low, and, in some cases, problem solving is not possible. Therefore, we propose the enhancement of SUHRL by constraining the exploration of sub goals based on the number of steps required to transition between them. This improvement is based on Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning with a k-step Adjacency Constraint, a method that can achieve efficient learning when sub goals are predefined. Experimental results using the Frozen Lake environment show that the proposed method exhibits a better learning efficiency than SUHRL.

articleTitle: A Study on the Effects of ICL and CoT Prompts on the Reward Function Generation of a Small Language Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This study explored methods to improve the success rate of reward function generation, a crucial task in robotic reinforcement learning, by applying In-Context Learning (ICL) and Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting techniques to a Small Language Model (SLM). While the existing reward function generation framework, Eureka, used OpenAI's Large Language Model, GPT-4, this study focused on generating reward functions using the LLaMA3 8B model, which can be implemented on an edge device. The experimental results showed that the CoT technique alone was insufficient to enhance the performance. However, partial improvements were observed when the ICL technique was employed. Notably, combining ICL with CoT prompting techniques consistently maintained the success rate of reward function generation in both the cartpole and ball balance tasks. This could be interpreted as the complementary effects of the two techniques, where the ICL technique provided the model with context related to reward function generation and the CoT technique facilitated the solution of complex problems through step-by-step reasoning. Therefore, it was concluded that integrating various prompting techniques was crucial to improving the performance of SLM -based reward function generation. Future research should focus on increasing the experimental samples to derive statistically significant results; refining the combination of ICL generalization methods with CoT to reduce errors; and applying various prompting techniques to find the optimal strategy.

articleTitle: Braille Character Recognition Independent of Lighting Direction Using Object Detection Models
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Braille text is widely used around the world as a means of communication for the visually impaired. Although Braille is often regarded as a tool for the visually impaired, there are instances where sighted individuals may want to verify Braille documents. For example, teachers at schools for the visually impaired may need to check homeworks or assignments written in Braille, or care workers supporting the daily lives of visually impaired people may need to verify Braille documents. To meet such social demands, optical Braille recognition (OBR) technologies have typically been developed using cameras and scanners. In particular, methods using object detection models based on Deep Learning have achieved high accuracy in recent years. Since Braille is represented by embossed dots on thick paper, the appearance of shadows varies greatly depending on the angle of the lighting. Therefore, the angle and intensity of the light significantly affect the accuracy of Braille recognition. Specifically, in the case of double-sided Braille, where Braille is embossed on both sides, it is necessary to distinguish between raised and recessed dots. Previous studies have mostly imposed constraints on the angle of illumination, such as limiting the imaging method to scanners or requiring the light source to be positioned on the top of the Braille document when using a camera. However, for practical use in daily life, it is preferable to recognize Braille documents regardless of the direction and lighting conditions. In this study, we created a dataset of Braille images captured under various angle of lighting and developed a Braille recognition model that is independent of the lighting angle by fine-tuning the object recognition model. We implemented and compared RetinaNet, which has been used in previous research, and the anchor-free model YOLOX as object detection models. As a result, we achieved a model capable of detecting Braille images with an accuracy of mAP50=O.98 or higher, regardless of the angle of lighting.

articleTitle: Preliminary Analysis of an Arm-Worn Device for Indicating Directions through Tactile Sensation
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: During the COVID-19 pandemic, face-to-face interactions were particularly limited in hospitals and elderly care facilities. Although telecommunication environments are increasing, they are mainly limited to audio and visual communication. Tactile sensation, which can act on emotions, is difficult to convey through telecommunication environments. Therefore, it is essential to use tactile senses as well as audiovisual senses to achieve “warm” communication. This study proposes an arm-mounted tactile presentation device consisting of several rollers. We focus on designing “pulling” and “stroking” motions among various tactile representations and conducted preliminary experiments of “pulling” motions. The experimental results show that the proposed device can convey pulling sensations from various directions.

articleTitle: Subjective Evaluation of Dialogues with Dyadic and Triadic Interactions Using a ChatGPT-Based Dialogue System
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: We investigated subjective evaluation of dialogues with dyadic and triadic interactions by a questionnaire. This system uses ChatGPT-based conversation with a facial expression function. In terms of human developmental stages, communication on triadic interaction is more advanced than on dyadic interaction. However, dialogue on triadic interaction was not evaluated as better necessarily. On dyadic interaction, most subjects evaluated this system as a good partner. On triadic interaction, half of the subjects evaluated this system as a very good partner who listened carefully, while another half evaluated as a poor partner because they couldn't communicate well. We estimate the reason of this negative evaluation is that the dialogue structure, which was designed to resemble interpersonal communication, required communication effort from the subjects, and they could find that a burden.

articleTitle: The Effect of Different Experimental Settings on Off- Policy Evaluations
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Ahstract-Counterfactual Machine Learning (CFML) is ma-chine learning for capturing data that could have been observed but was not actually observed. Off-policy evaluation (OPE) is one of the research areas of CFML, which aims to evaluate a hypothetical policy using operational data from another policy. This approach enables the evaluation of a new policy's performance without the need for risky and costly online experiments. Although various OPE methods have been proposed, the accuracy with which each OPE method evaluates a policy depends on the environment setting of the domain in which it is applied, so it is not possible to measure the performance of a method using only one experimental environment. Therefore, it is necessary to eval-uate OPE methods using multiple experimental environments. In this study, we conducted performance evaluation exper-iments of three basic OPE methods in different experimental environments, and discussed how environmental factors affect the accuracy of the OPE methods.

articleTitle: On Some Variants for Anticlustering
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Anticlustering involves partitioning objects into groups such that intergroup similarity is high and intragroup heterogeneity is high. In this paper, we propose five methods for anticlustering. The first proposed method minimizes the distances between group means. The second method minimizes both the distances between group means and those among group variances. The remaining three methods minimize the divergence among the distributions of groups using the Kullback-Leibler divergence, Jeffreys divergence, and Wasserstein distance. Through numerical experiments using an artificial dataset, the latter three methods prove superior to the others and the two conventional methods in terms of anticlustering quality and the perspective of parameter setting.

articleTitle: Selection of Gubbins for Wind Turbine Blades Using Fuzzy WASPAS Method
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Wind energy is the primary source of electricity, which is environmentally friendly. The wind turbine helps to generate wind energy, and the blades used in wind turbines play a vital role because the rotation of the turbine depends on the gubbins that are used to manufacture the blades. Hence while selecting gubbins it is necessary to give more weightage to particular features like density, tensile strength, stiffness, costs, environmental resistance, etc., The relative importance of alternatives concerning criteria may not be precise in general. So the formulation in terms of fuzzy logic is required to make it precise. Therefore this study carries out the selection of gubbins for wind turbine blades using one of the Fuzzy Multi Criteria Decision Making (MCDM) methods. Fuzzy Weighted Aggregated Sum Product Assessment (Fuzzy WASPAS) is one of the decision-making (MCDM) methods that combines the Fuzzy Weighted Sum Model (Fuzzy WSM) and Fuzzy Weighted Product Model (Fuzzy WPM) and gives the aggregated value. This method uses unclear data and solves the problem by finding the best alternatives.

Author Keywords: Fuzzy Weighted Aggregated Sum Product Assessment

articleTitle: Handwritten Character String Recognition Using Transformer and CNN Features
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: While character recognition systems applications with restrictions on writing conditions, such as zip code recognition and ledger sheet recognition, are in practical use, the accuracy of free handwritten character string recognition is still low and there are many challenges. Japanese free handwritten character strings are difficult to segment because some Japanese characters consist of multiple connected components and there are no spaces between words. Therefore, in this study, we propose a method for handwritten character string recognition method that does not require character segmentation using Transformer and CNN features. Transformer-based models usually require a large amount of annotated training data. However, our method can be trained with a small amount of annotated training data. Comparative experiments confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method by achieving CER=O.127 while CRNN [1] and TrOCR [2] achieve CER=O.562 and CER=O.174, respectively. The results show that the proposed method is effective for Japanese character string recognition, where the variety of character strings is large and it is difficult to secure a sufficient number of training samples for each character string.

articleTitle: Head Pose Estimation Using a Chest-Mounted Camera and Its Evaluation Based on CG Images
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In everyday life, we naturally turn our heads or focus our gaze on objects of interest. By capturing a person's head pose or gaze direction, it is possible to record their actions and identify the objects they are focusing on. This study proposes a head pose estimation to infer and document the objects of interest based on head movements. We utilize a camera mounted on the user's chest and develop a deep-learning model to estimate head pose from the captured images. The training data was generated using a CG model, and the model's performance was validated.

articleTitle: Multimodal Optimization by Speciation-Based Differential Evolution using Graphs with Stochastic Global and Local Searches and Crossover
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Multimodal optimization is a very difficult task to search for all optimal solutions at once in optimization problems with multiple optimal solutions. Speciation using proximity graphs has been proposed for multimodal optimization. In multimodal optimization, it is necessary to first discover many candidates of optimal solutions by global search, and then to converge to optimal solutions using local search. In this study, the speciation-based differential evolution using graphs (SDE- G) is improved by introducing βRNG, a stochastic change from global search to local search, and a crossover operation. By using βRN G, it is possible to first discover many candidates of optimal solutions using the coarse graph, and to gradually narrow down the candidates using the dense graph. Since it is difficult to decide when to switch from global to local search, we propose a stochastic switch as the search progresses. Also, the crossover operation with adaptive crossover rate is proposed to generate new solutions by combining elements of good candidates. The performance of the proposed method is shown by optimizing well-known benchmark problems for “CEC'2013 special session and competition on niching methods for multimodal function optimization”.

articleTitle: Extraction of Handwriting Features in Tablet Shape Drawing for Developmental Screening
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In recent years, there has been an increasing demand for more easily accessible testing tools for developmental screening because the number of certified public psychologists and testing institutions is limited. To solve the problems, we have focused on drawing tests for screening and developed a tablet-type drawing data acquisition system to collect drawing data from young children. In this study, we investigate the relationship between developmental age and features extracted from stroke data in drawing. Specifically, based on the pen tip's position with each elapsed time from the test's start, we extracted each drawn figure's features, such as speed during drawing, for performing a multiple regression analysis using these features and living age in months as an explanatory variable and developmental age in months as the objective variable. As a result, we found that living age in months contributed the most to estimating developmental age in months.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control Based on Estimated Dynamics With Extended State Observer and Its Application of Quadrotor
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This study considered a method of applying model predictive control (MPC) to a system whose dynamics are unknown, using the dynamics estimated by an extended state observer (ESO). In our approach, the dynamics required to calculate MPC are estimated using ESO, which can estimate the dynamic characteristics of the plant as a total disturbance. MPC can be applied without a detailed model by using the dynamics obtained by ESO as a predictive model. The effectiveness of the proposed method was confirmed through simulations on a quadrotor.

articleTitle: Effects of Intelligence Test Training Between Robots and University Students
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In recent years, as the percentage of children with developmental disabilities in general education classrooms has increased, so has the need for clinical psychologists to administer psychological tests. There are two types of training methods for psychological testing: classroom training and field training. However, due to difficulties in securing training sites and subjects, there is no environment in which clinical psychologists can receive sufficient training in psychological testing. Therefore, this study develops a child-like robot that can train clinical psychologists in intelligence testing (hereinafter referred to as the “proposed robot”). The proposed robot is equipped with the same speech content as that of a child undergoing intelligence testing. The clinical psychologist trains the robot to perform the intelligence test by talking to the robot. This paper investigates the learning effects of training with a proposed robot on university students studying to become clinical psychologists. The experimental results suggest that training with the proposed robot has the same learning effect as learning to read a conventional manual.

articleTitle: Implementing Network Transformation Based Algorithms for a Special Case of Scheduling Jobs with Periodic Due Dates on Parallel Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In this paper, we revisit a scheduling problem of just-in-time jobs with periodic due dates on parallel identical machines with multiple service slots, and address a novel imple-mentation issue of a network transformation based exact algorithm for a polynomially solvable case. Due to the periodic just-in-time constraint and a restriction on service slot occupation, the number of service slots required for processing each job can be viewed as a virtual processing time of the job. The special case of polynomially solvable contains two kinds of jobs such that one kind of a job requires exactly one service slot for the processing, and the other kind of a job requires two consecutive service slots, and further the number of the second kind of jobs is assumed to be a fixed integer. The objective is to minimize the total charge, which is a variant of the total weighted completion time. Any instance of the special case of the scheduling problem is known to be equivalently transformed to a series of instances of the minimum cost flow problem, and an exact algorithm for the minimum cost flow problem can find an optimal solution for the special case of the scheduling problem in polynomial time. In this paper, we implement the network transformation based exact algorithm, and attempt to estimate the service slot, in which each job of the second kind is completed in an optimal solution, for reducing the execution time of the network transformation based exact algorithm. We also demonstrate the quality of the estimation of service slot empirically, and report the numerical results.

articleTitle: Prediction Of Power Demand And Factor Identification Using Sparse Modeling AI With Ensemble Learning For Improvement Of Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: We have been using sparse modeling AI to identify factors and predict in power demand. In this research, we applied ensemble learning to further improve the accuracy by integrating the results of multiple models. Experimental results showed that sparse modeling AI identified the demand factors, and ensemble learning achieved an average absolute prediction error of 7.5%.

articleTitle: Theoretical Analysis of Transmission Characteristics in PORC-OFDM Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: The objective of the PORC-OFDM proposed by the authors is to suppress the reduction of transmission rate when the number of repeatedly transmitted symbols is increased to improve communication quality. In this study, theoretical analysis is used to gain a bird's-eye view of the overall of the wireless communication channel, and to derive a theoretical formula for the bit error rate (BER) of the PORC-OFDM over AWGN channels by treating the modulation scheme and conditions of the wireless communication channel as parameters. The BER obtained by the derived theoretical equation are compared with those obtained by computer simulation to clarify their validity. The BER of the PORC-OFDM is also compared with that of the RC-OFDM at the same transmission rate using the derived theoretical equation, and the superiority of the PORC-OFDM is quantitatively verified.

articleTitle: Aperiodic Multivariate Time-Series Generative Adversarial Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: We propose a multivariate time-series generative adversarial network (GAN) called aperiodic multivariate time-series GAN (AMTGAN) to improve the forecasting GAN (ForGAN) for obtaining uncertainty-aware predictions from real-world data. The gated recurrent unit (GRU) used in the conventional ForGAN generators and discriminators fails to properly model periodicity because every timestep is treated equally. In AMTGAN, we apply a multivariate time-series predictive model called dual self-attention network to both periodic and aperiodic data to extend the original ForGAN. As a result, the proposed AMTGAN can reach accurate predictions on both periodic and aperiodic data.

articleTitle: Tomato Fruit Evolution and Maturity estimation from RGB Time-lapse Observation via Modern Structure from Motion and Instance Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In various cultivation environments, monitoring fruit development, such as phenotyping, is crucial to optimise and enhance plant and environmental conditions. A statistical approach is introduced in combination with computer vision to estimate tomato fruit maturity features, such as size and shape, from a set of sequential RGB images. An novel end-to-end routine has been implemented to locate and measure the size and colour of tomato fruit from handheld image sequences. This is achieved through a combination of instance segmentation and modern Structure from Motion (SfM) methods. Our approach is time-efficient and easy to implement in both small gardens and large greenhouse environments. Measuring tomato fruit size by hand, for example with a calliper, is limited by the symmetry of the fruit shape. In addition to estimating the fruit diameter, we can measure deviations from the targeted spherical topology with millimetre precision and incorporate any morphological abnormalities.

articleTitle: Filtrate Estimation from Filter Press Process in a Water Treatment Facility based on Image Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Sludge dewatering is a crucial process in water treatment facilities, aimed at reducing moisture content to produce concentrated sludge, known as cake. This study focuses on the filter press process, employing a fixed camera to capture images of the filtrate-the water expelled from the filter press. The purpose of this study is to estimate the filtrate volume from these images and compare the estimates with actual measurements. In our image processing, image thresholding is used for segmentation, isolating the water area and counting its pixels. In our data analysis, Spearman Rank Correlation reveals a strong relationship (correlation coefficient = 0.97) between pixel count and filtrate volume. Additionally, quadratic polynomial regression provides accurate filtrate estimations, which are very useful for predicting the stop timing of the dewatering process.

articleTitle: Development of a Virtual Patient Model for Kampo Medical Interview: New Approach for Enhancing Empathy and Understanding of Kampo Medicine Pathological Concepts
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Global interest in complementary and alternative medicine has increased in recent years, with Kampo medicine in Japan gaining greater trust and use. Detailed patient interviews are essential in Kampo medicine, as the physician's empathy is critical to diagnostic precision. Typically, medical students develop empathy and deepen their understanding of Kampo's pathological concepts through clinical practice. However, the COVID-19 pandemic has imposed significant restrictions on clinical training. To address this challenge, we propose a novel educational approach to enhance empathy and understanding of Kampo medicine by developing a virtual patient application. This application leverages generative artificial intelligence to simulate realistic patient interactions, enabling students to practice Kampo medical interviews in a safe, controlled environment. The AI-generated conversations are designed to reflect the emotional nuances of real-life dialogue, with the virtual patients' facial expressions synchronized to these emotions, thus enhancing the realism of the training. The suggested method allows repeated practice at any time and fosters the development of essential diag-nostic and empathetic skills. While promising challenges remain in improving these simulations' accuracy, further refinements are still under consideration.

articleTitle: Learning Effects of Programming Educational Board Game in Collaborative Learning between Robots and Humanities Students
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
