abstract: In recent years, programming education has become a mandatory component of the curriculum in elementary, junior high, and high schools. In this context, numerous educational institutions are employing board games that facilitate the teaching of programming thinking. The advantages of board games include the ability to learn in a stress-free environment while engaging in collaborative play, which can stimulate a desire to learn. However, board games inherently require the presence of an opponent to play with, and the opponent is not always at home. Consequently, this study developed an educational support robot to play programming education board games with students. The experiment investigated the learning effects of playing against this robot on college students who had no prior experience with programming. The results indicated that competing against the robot provided higher learning effectiveness for college students compared to competing against human opponents.

articleTitle: Psychological Analysis of Right-Turn Driving Behavior for Development of Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In this paper, the right-turn behavior at a left-hand traffic intersection was analyzed in order to control autonomous vehicles not only for a safe drive but also for a drive that does not cause discomfort to occupants of both the autonomous vehicle and the surrounding vehicles. The trend of the decision to make a right turn was investigated at an intersection where there were a vehicle turning right and a vehicle oncoming straight focusing on discomfort of occupants of both vehicles. The results suggested the importance of considering psychological aspects.

articleTitle: A Pilot Valve Endoscopic Image Inspection System Using Unsupervised Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In production lines, chips and burrs are sometimes left inside the casing of pilot valves, necessitating internal inspections. As the inside of the casing cannot be seen directly, the inside is photographed using an endoscopic camera. The images captured are then visually inspected by the inspector, one by one. This paper proposes an endoscopic image inspection system designed to detect abnormalities from the images taken inside by an endoscopic camera.

articleTitle: Discrimination between command and drawing strokes for sketch-based CAD interfaces based on fuzzy spline curve fragmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a command stroke (CS)/ drawing stroke (DS) discriminator that distinguishes input penstrokes into CS for command input and DS for geometric-shape input, with the aim of realizing command input by penstrokes in sketch-based computer-aided design (CAD) interfaces. This discriminator utilizes the fuzzy spline curve fragmentation, and is characterized by its ability to discriminate in real-time without relying on textual information or geometric features. By introducing the discriminator into a sketch-based CAD interface and experimentally implementing several command inputs, we demonstrated through drawing experiments that both the command and geometric-shape inputs can be implemented seamlessly with sketch-based input to efficiently complete technical drawings.

articleTitle: Predicting Joint Movement Trajectories from the ECoG Signal Patterns of Apes*
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Due to a strong heterogeneity between two signals, it is often a challenging problem to obtain an analytical model between brain signals and joint movements. This paper proposes an approach to predicting joint movement from electrocorticography via a convolutional neural network. First, spectrogram images were obtained in sequence from the measured ECoG of an ape by sliding a time-window. Next, the corresponding joint movement of the ape was extracted from video recording by applying DeepLabCut. Finally, the spectrogram images and the joint movement were utilized as an input and a desired output to train the convolutional neural network, respectively. The result showed the feasibility of the proposed approach to model a relationship between the electrocorticography and the joint movements.

articleTitle: Enhancing Machine Learning Interpretability Through a Graphical User Interface
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In designing machine learning algorithms, there is a balance to be struck between interpretability and performance. Typically, simpler algorithms that are easier for humans to understand tend to have lower classification performance compared to more complex and less transparent ones. Over the years, several methods have been proposed to minimize this trade-off as much as possible. This paper builds on a previous study that introduced a partially explainable classifier using white and black box models. It presents a simple graphic user interface (GUI) specifically designed for human users to better understand the mentioned classifier. This paper provides an overview and a few experimental results acquired using the GUI.

articleTitle: Impressions of Agents Encouraging Humans to Adopt Intentional Stance by Refraining from Action
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This study investigated the impressions that agents refraining from action give to humans. As interactions between humans and agents become more common, agents are increasingly required to exhibit cooperative behavior. In human communication, refraining from an action out of consideration for others is frequently seen as cooperative behavior (referred to as enryo in Japan). However, few studies have investigated how this agent behavior affects human impressions of the agent. Thus, we developed an experimental virtual environment where humans and agents engage in cooperative tasks, including scenarios with refraining and non-refraining agents. We examined whether humans perceive the refraining agents as demonstrating enryo. The results indicate that humans tend to view the refraining agent as demonstrating enryo and find it more anthropomorphic and likeable than the non-refraining agent.

articleTitle: Survival Time Prediction of Patients with Soft Tissue Tumor Using Biopsy Pathological Images
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Malignant soft tissue tumor are rare cancers and uncommon diseases. Ideally, rare cancers should be diagnosed by a pathologist who specializes in that organ, but there is a chronic shortage of pathologists in Japan. Pathological diagnosis by artificial intelligence (AI) is required to improve the reliability of diagnosis and to support pathological diagnosis of rare diseases. There are several studies to predict the prognosis of cancer patients using pathology images, but most of them requires a large dataset and capable machine learning model such as convolutional neural networks (CNN). Since soft tissue tumors are rare diseases, large datasets cannot be collected, and existing approaches would not perform enough for clinical diagnosis. Therefore, this paper proposes a survival time prediction method using unsupervised machine learning algorithms that extracts pathological image feature by autoencoder, and K-means clustering and K Nearest Neighbor (KNN) regression perform the survival time prediction based on the extracted image features. The experiments on 27 soft tissue tumor patients showed that the proposed method predicted the survival time with an average error of 17.89 months.

articleTitle: Contact Lens Automatic Optical Inspection Method Based on YOLOv9
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Traditional inspection methods for contact lenses primarily involved manual examination, where workers directly assessed the physical properties and manufacturing defects of the lenses. Consequently, the quality determination relied on the workers' judgment, leading to inconsistencies. In order to address this issue, although Automated Optical Inspection (AOI) was introduced, it has limitations in applying to various types of contact lenses. As part of research to utilize deep learning in AOI, this paper introduces a You Only Look Once (YOLO) v9-based contact lens inspection technique that leverages a small dataset of contact lens images. This method involves training YOLO v9 with the limited number of images that include various defects such as bubbles, cracks, and foreign particles, as well as images of defect-free contact lenses.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Public Bicycle Usage Patterns between Seoul's ‘Ttareungi’ and New York's ‘Citi Bike’
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This paper analyzes and compares the factors influencing the use of public bicycles in Seoul's ‘Ttareungi’ and New York's ‘Citi Bike,’ which operate within distinct cultural, environmental, and regional contexts, enabling a unique comparative study. A multiple regression analysis and a random forest analysis were performed using rental history data from both ‘Ttareungi’ and ‘Citi Bike’ as dependent variables. Independent variables included environmental factors such as weather and seasonal conditions. This study assesses the impact of these factors on bicycle usage behavior. Analysis results highlighted the significant influence of seasonal changes and weekend/holiday variables on public bicycle usage. Although both models yielded significant results, the random forest analysis demonstrated better accuracy and revealed distinct patterns in the importance of certain variables. The variation in coefficient values and variable importance between the two areas indicates that while environmental factors similarly affect bicycle usage patterns, regional climatic conditions have distinct influences. This paper proposes that incorporating variables such as personal and economic characteristics in future research could further enhance the analysis and help to develop strategies to promote public bicycle use.

articleTitle: Distinguishing Identical Pills in Unit-Dose Packages with Balanced Data
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This study aims to develop a system for detecting medical errors in unit dose packaging (UDP). The system compares the contents of subsequent UDPs to the first package in a series, which serves as a reference to ensure consistency in the pills contained. This preliminary study focuses on verifying whether the pills in each UDP match those in the reference package. The process begins with the application of YOLOv8 to detect pills within the UDP. Semantic segmentation is employed to isolate the pills, followed by the creation of modified images to facilitate feature extraction. Subsequently, a dataset is created from the extracted features to train the model. Feature selection methods are applied to identify the most effective features for classifying the pills as identical or not. The results indicate the effectiveness of the proposed feature extraction method for the intended system. The balance of the data is found to be crucial in determining pill identity. The highest F1-score achieved in this study was 0.961, demonstrating the efficacy of the method.

articleTitle: A Denoising Method from Low-dose CT Images Based on Improved U-Net with Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Japan has the highest number of CT scanners per million population among developed countries, and the annual medical radiation dose is about four times the world average. Screening of high-risk populations with low-dose CT has been shown to reduce lung cancer mortality. However, in order to obtain image quality comparable to that of normal-dose CT, it is necessary to accurately estimate the image noise of low-dose CT. In this paper, we apply a noise reduction method using convolutional neural networks: the CNN model is based on U-Net, a fully convolutional network with encoder-decoder structure, with two convolutional layer modifications and three attention mechanisms. Experimental results using whole body slice CT images of piglets show that the proposed method is useful by comparing with CT images of normal dose and by evaluating image quality using peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR).

articleTitle: A Novel MRI Brain Tumor Detection Method Incorporated Residual Dendritic Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In this study, we present a novel method for brain tumor detection that emphasizes dendritic learning for feature mapping. We use the RegNet module to extract high-quality features from brain MRI images, capturing complex features and structures effectively. These features are then classified using a custom-designed dendritic neuron model, which leverages the principles of dendritic learning to achieve high accuracy. To evaluate the performance of the proposed method, we conduct extensive experiments on a benchmark brain tumor dataset. The results demonstrate that our method significantly enhances classification accuracy. Our findings suggest that integrating advanced feature extraction modules like RegNet with dendritic learning-based classification neurons can greatly improve the performance of brain tumor detection systems. This study opens new avenues for further research in developing efficient and accurate neural network architectures for various medical image processing tasks.

articleTitle: SynthSearch: An information retrieval system visualizing diverse perspectives based on dialectics
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In recent years, excessive recommendation functions in search systems have led to the emergence of biased opinions and social division. Although it is important to present users with diverse perspectives, people tend to avoid information that differs from their own beliefs, demonstrating the phenomenon known as confirmation bias. In this paper, we attempt to reduce this bias by applying the concept of dialectics. In order to incorporate dialectics into the system, we introduce a map-type search system that represents comments on social media using nodes and edges, allowing users to see relationships between comments based on the colors of the edges. We conduct a comparative experiment between a structure with conflicting relationships and a dialectical structure. As a result, we find that people are more receptive to antithetical information in the group presented with dialectical information than in that presented with conflicting information. Thus, we expect dialectics to reduce the influence of confirmation bias.

articleTitle: Automatic Generation of Soundscapes Based on Spatio-Temporal Keywords and Elucidation of Soundscapes' Impact on Human Reading Experience
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: We present a method for converting text into soundscapes, automatically generating synthesized soundscapes for text that include sound objects and descriptions of sound effects. Previous research often focused on objects in text but neglected descriptive details, leading to a mismatch between the audible effect of generated soundscape and textual description. Our system maps spatio-temporal keywords to sound effects, creating soundscapes that closely align with written narratives. We conducted subjective evaluation experiments with 24 participants, demonstrating that the soundscapes generated by proposed system with effects that more accurately reflect textual descriptions compared to existing model. Additionally, we conducted reading experiments to explore potential applications of the text-to-audio (TTA) task, a topic previously unaddressed. The results indicate that text-based soundscapes enhance the reading experience in both silent and aloud reading scenarios.

articleTitle: Method for Classifying Emotions in Older Adults Playing eSports
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In recent years, extending the healthy lifespan of older adults has become increasingly important; however, dementia is a major hindrance to achieving this goal. Electronic sports (eSports) are receiving increasing attention owing to their potential to prevent dementia. People experience various emotions while participating in eSports. When quantified, these emotions can serve as an indicator of how much participants enjoy the game and can be used to evaluate eSports. This study investigates methods for estimating emotional arousal from videos of participants playing eSports and classify these emotions into positive and negative categories. We used changes in the saturation in both cheek areas of the face during emotional events as inputs for a machine learning model. This model combined a convolutional neural network and a long short-term memory network. The results suggest that using saturation information from both cheeks as features in machine learning can potentially classify emotions into two types: positive and negative. We believe this method can be a key technology for extending the healthy lifespan of older adults and supporting remote communication.

articleTitle: Frequency Analysis for Measuring Tremor with VR Nose-Finger Test Based on Optical Device
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Ataxia is caused by brain damage such as stroke or head trauma, and the muscles become unable to work in a coordinated manner even though there is no paralysis or loss of consciousness. A symptom of ataxia is tremor, which is an involuntary, rhythmic, vibratory movement. Such tremors affect daily movements and work, leading to a decrease in quality of life (QOL). Effective rehabilitation and identification of symptoms and disorders are important for improving such symptoms. However, in the Nose-Finger Test, which is one of the tests performed by physical therapists, there are concerns that the inter-rater reliability and clinical services will decrease because the evaluation is subjective. In addition, virtual reality (VR) equipment has developed in recent years and has become more common in our lives. Accordingly, VR rehabilitation is being developed. Therefore, in this study, we used the VR Nose-Finger Test, analyzed the frequency at the time of measurement to extract features depending on the presence of symptoms are present, and performed discrimination using machine learning to evaluate the effectiveness. As a result, differences depending on the presence of symptoms were observed from the frequency, and the effectiveness of machine learning judgment was demonstrated.

articleTitle: Extraction of c- F os Protein Regions from Mouse Brain Slice Images using Multi-channelization, 1 x 1 Convolution and U -Net
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This study proposed a novel extraction method of c-Fos protein regions in DAB(3,3‘-diaminobenzidine)-stained mouse brain slice images using the U-Net model combined with the multi-channelization and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\times 1$</tex> convolution techniques. Our U-Net m odel, called <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\times 1$</tex> conv U-Net, was applied to three DAB- strainedmouse slice images whose resolutions were <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1000\mathrm{x}1000$</tex> pixels. The experimental results demonstrated that the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\times 1$</tex> conv U-Net outperformed the conventional U-Net.

articleTitle: CAFTTA: Mitigating Unseen Class Forgetting in Test-Time Adaptation with Knowledge Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In real-world applications, deployed deep learning models often encounter test data from domains significantly different from their training data. This domain shift typically results in performance degradation for conventional deep learning models. Test-time adaptation (TTA) has emerged as a promising research direction to address this challenge by adapting models during test-time to unpredictable domains. However, in real-world scenarios, data could exhibit different class distributions as well as domains. Consequently, models are deployed in environments where they temporarily cannot observe data of a particular class. Under these conditions, test-time adaptation methods exhibit catastrophic forgetting of unseen class, significantly compromising their ability to generalize. To address this critical issue, we propose Class Anti-Forgetting Test-Time Adaptation (CAFTTA). Our method shares domain knowledge by weight sharing between the original source model and the test-time adaptation model, and preserves knowledge of unseen classes through entropy-based knowledge fusion. Our method minimizes performance degradation on seen classes while preventing unseen class forgetting. Experimentally, we demonstrate that our method significantly mitigates the unseen class forgetting problem faced by existing test time adaptation methods in both static and continuous domain scenarios.

articleTitle: Two-Dimensional Display-Based the Proteus Effect on Muscle Activity Level
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: The Proteus effect is a psychological and physical change caused by the perception of an avatar as a substitute for oneself in a VR space. In our previous study, we showed that not only VR space but also an avatar projected on a two-dimensional display reduced subjective fatigue during squatting exercise. In this paper, we investigate whether physical fatigue during squatting exercise changes in addition to subjective fatigue by measuring surface EMG. In addition, we explore the influence on the Proteus effect when the subject selects an avatar that is “close to the ideal avatar” for himselflherself. The avatar conditions were “muscular,” “non-muscular,” and “no avatar (own appearance),” and we prepared and compared a group of subjects who selected the ideal body shape and a group of subjects who did not select the ideal body shape. Our findings showed that, in the group that did not select the avatar condition, the subjective fatigue level was significantly lower in the muscular avatar condition than in the other conditions, as in the previous study. On the other hand, there was no significant difference in physical fatigue between the two groups. This suggests that the use of muscular avatar, instead of selecting the ideal avatar, results in less subjective fatigue and is as effective as other training.

articleTitle: Distance-Based Subset Selection With a Knee Point for Multi-Objective Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Recently, the use of an unbounded external archive in the design of evolutionary multi-objective optimization (EMO) algorithms has received increasing attention. An important component in the use of an unbounded external archive is its subset selection method used to select a pre-specified number of solutions from the archive. One of the most commonly used subset selection method is distance-based subset selection (DSS) since it is very easy to calculate and can easily scale to many-objective optimization. However, the DSS's selection mechanism usually lead to a small hypervolume value for the selected subset even when the optimal subset with respect to the minimum distance among the selected solutions is obtained. In this paper, we propose a modification to the DSS algorithm by selecting a knee point as the first solution. The knee point is often a solution of interest to decision makers in the absence of preference information. Experimental results show that the inclusion of a knee point generally has a positive effect on improving the hypervolume value of the selected subset.

articleTitle: Applying Burn-in Strategy to Deep Reinforcement Learning with Spiking Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In recent years, neural networks in deep reinforce-ment learning (D RL) have achieved success in various tasks, owing to their high expressiveness and flexibility. Neural networks are expected to be increasingly used for robot control. However, large neural networks consume a significant amount of power during training and operation. Given that the power supply that can be installed in robots is limited, challenges remain in the practical application of robot control using DRL, which includes large-scale neural networks. Conversely, spiking neural networks (SNNs) have high power efficiency, which is achieved through dedicated computational elements. Previous studies reported that SNNs can be applied to DRL to learn a robot's walking motion in a virtual environment and reduce energy consumption. Although previous studies have applied SNNs to DRL, they have the drawback of recursive computation, causing output delays. In this study, we propose a method that combines SNNs with a structure that addresses the issues of previous studies using a twin-delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3). In addition, a burn-in strategy was introduced to estimate the action values using the internal states of the SNNs. Experiments in a virtual environment showed that the proposed method achieved higher rewards than the previous methods.

articleTitle: Registration of Spinal Region on CT Images Based on SuperPoint with Convolutional Block Attention Module
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Cancer is currently the leading cause of death in Japan, and the number of cancer patients is increasing every year. The number of patients with bone metastases from cancer is also increasing. The spine is a common site of bone metastasis, and cancer metastasis to the spine can cause serious symptoms such as hypercalcaemia and nerve paralysis due to spinal cord compression. As a result, it can affect patients’ quality of life. Early detection and treatment of bone metastases is therefore important. To analyse the image information, CAD (Computer Aided Diagnosis) is introduced in image registration, which is obtained by temporal subtraction technique. One of them is CT (Computed Tomography) image-based registration technique by taken at different times of the same subject and performs subtraction to enhance changes in the lesion over time. In this approach, the registration of the same slice is important for the generation of temporal subtraction image. In this paper, we propose a method to register both images obtained different time series based on SuperPoint algorithm incorporated CBAM (Convolutional Block Attention Module) as a method to select the same slice and register the spinal region on the CT image.

articleTitle: LiDAR Information based High-Speed-High-Accuracy Object Recognition Network for Autonomous Vehicles*
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Rapid advances in in-vehicle technology are leading the automotive industry in a safer, more efficient, and intelligent direction. Object recognition technology based on LiDAR sensor information enables highly accurate object location detection and plays an important role in autonomous driving systems. However, there is a trade-off between detection speed and accuracy, and the need for object recognition methods that are both fast and accurate is high. In this study, we propose a method to achieve both detection speed and accuracy by improving CenterPoint [1]. The proposed method uses a lightweight deep learning network with attention mechanisms. It is expected to promote the spread and development of autonomous driving technology and contribute to further innovation in the automotive industry.

articleTitle: Measuring Fruit Diameter for Fruit Tree Management Purposes Using an RGB-D Camera
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: The number of farmers in Japan is declining owing to the aging of the farming population and the difficulty of managing high-quality fruit cultivation. Among the fruit tree management tasks, the fruit enlargement survey, which measures fruit diameter, examines the average size of fruit. However, because the survey using calipers is time-consuming, this study examined a method for detecting a fruit and calculating its diameter using an RGB-D camera.

articleTitle: Modeling of Weight Perception Based on Subjectivity by Considering Individual Differences
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: The minimum amount of perception that humans can perceive is called the stimulus threshold. This study aims to clarify the stimulus threshold of weight perception for the biceps brachii muscle based on a method of constant stimuli. In general, the stimulus threshold depends on the individual. The authors consider that physical characteristics are related to individual differences, construct a model of the relationship between physical characteristics and stimulus thresholds, and attempt to estimate stimulus thresholds from physical characteristics. The constructed model is evaluated via cross-validation and found to be able to estimate stimulus thresholds from physical characteristics with an 85% accuracy.

articleTitle: A Twin Dual-Arm Robot Testbed to Collect the Human Demonstration Data for Imitation Learning*
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Collecting consistent human demonstrations has been a problematic issue in the field of a learning from demonstration. This paper presents a twin dual-arm robot testbed to collect human demonstration data while performing manual tasks in the activities of daily livings such as opening/closing a window, opening-up/closing-down a sauce bottle cap, etc. The testbed consists of the two sets of a dual-arm robot; for each robot, one-side arm has 6-DoF with a crab-gripper as its hand. Two dual-arm robots are mounted at the front and back of a table-type station. A human operator performs actions to complete a given task with the one at the back; the human operator's actions, meanwhile, are duplicated by the other robot at the front simultaneously. The experimental results show the testbed's potential to gather consistent human demonstration data for training a machine learning agent to manipulate the dual-arm robot under an imitation learning framework.

articleTitle: Simulation Results of a Spatio-Temporal Perplexion Estimation Method Based on Learners' Facial Expression Changes
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In recent years, the field of I'CT education has emerged, and the research and development of educational support robots has attracted significant interest. In this study, we focus on a perplexity estimation method for educational support robots that estimates perplexity based on learners' facial expressions. The conventional method for estimating perplexion from facial expressions at a given time is not yet sufficiently accurate. It is believed that the accuracy of the method can be improved by using not only facial expressions at a given time but also time-series data on changes in facial expressions between that time and the previous time. This study focuses on a perplexion estimation method for educational support robots that estimates perplexion based on the facial expressions of learners. The objective of this study is to verify the accuracy of the spatio-temporal perplexion estimation method through simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Measuring Changes in Posture While Walking Using a Inertial Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Postural measurements of the upper body are commonly made by radiography or optical methods; radiography requires special facilities. Measurement by camera is difficult to estimate feature points on the spine. Inertial sensors are small and portable and do not have the drawbacks. In this study, we conduct an accuracy experiment and the walking test of the inertial sensor. The walking test was conducted with normal walking and walking with a load attached to the foot, and the features were compared by frequency analysis. Result of the walking test. The development of this system is expected to classify healthy subjects and pathological patients.

articleTitle: A Note on Even-Sized Spectral Clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Clustering is a typical unsupervised learning method for classifying unsupervised data. One of the clustering meth-ods, even-sized clustering based on optimization (ECBO), is a clustering algorithm that imposes a constraint to equalize the size of each cluster. ECBO has been suggested to be effective in delivery and other problems. However, it is limited to Euclidean space. On the other hand, spectral clustering with a wide range of applicability for partitioning graph data has been proposed. In this paper, we propose even-sized spectral clustering, which imposes a size-equal constraint on spectral clustering, and show that it is an extension of the graph partitioning problem. We also verify the validity of the results through numerical examples.

articleTitle: Scalability Evaluation of zk-SNARK Authentication in Blockchain-Based E-Voting
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Blockchain-based e-voting requires a robust voter authentication module to support its functionality and implementation. Scalability issues in e-voting systems, blockchain technology, and voter authentication modules combined altogether render the mass adoption and use of blockchain-based e-voting systems either partial or fully decentralized not feasible. This work studies a zk-SNARK authentication module for voter identity verification and validation in a blockchain-based e-voting application. The load testing was conducted to observe the system's throughput, speedup, and efficiency under two scenarios: with and without a load balancer, as implementing a blockchain-based e-voting might be partially decentralized with government intervention in certain parts of the process. The zk-SNARK authentication module studied in this work preserves users' privacy and eliminates the need for a password-based authentication system. However, the scalability evaluation shows a sub-linear speedup and efficiency of the zk-SNARK authentication module, leading to poor system scalability.

articleTitle: Spatiotemporal Comparison of Brain Activities Between Quadruped Image Recognition and Recalling Processes
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Otsuki had conducted categorical naming tasks on aphasia patients with categorical naming disorder, and reported a case in which the difference in performance was shown between “round objects” and “non-round objects”, and showed that visual elements such as shape may have some influence on the recalling process. Yamanoi et al. had presented images of a quadruped animal and measured EEGs from the subjects during recalling their names. The equivalent current dipole localization (ECDL) estimation was done to these EEGs. As a result, activities were estimated in areas related to visual cortex, memory, language cortex, etc., such as V1, hippocampus, and Broca's area. In images of typical animals with almost round shape, such as dogs and bears, brain activity was not estimated in the right angular gyrus (An G), but brain activity was estimated in the right AnG in atypical animals such as giraffes. In this study, the authors measured the EEGs from five subjects during the image recognition process of quadrupeds as well as during the recalling name process of them. After analysis of EEGs by the ECDL method, they compared the activities between two processes. In case of the image recognition process, no activity on the right angular gyrus was observed in dogs in common with all subjects. For images of giraffe, brain activity was observed on the right angular gyrus for all subjects, and these tendencies were the same to those of the estimated brain activity. But activities were observed on the right angular gyrus for bear and lion in some subjects. And in case of the recalling name process, brain activity was observed on the right angular gyrus in all subjects for image of giraffe. No activity on the right angular gyrus was observed for round shape quadruped in common with all subjects on the right angular gyrus, except only one estimation for one subject.

articleTitle: Case Study on a Navigation System using Growing Neural Gas
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to develop a navigation method for illuminance-measuring robots that can traverse nar-row paths, such as doors, to achieve fully automated operation. In this paper, a navigation system based on Growing Neural Gas (GNG) is incorporated into the conventional automated control of illuminance-measuring robots. First, we review the conventional control using fuzzy control and multi-objective behavioral mediation techniques to verify whether the updated system can navigate smoothly through narrow corridors. Next, the integration and effectiveness of the GNG-based navigation system will be demonstrated through real-world experiments to confirm that the system can navigate narrow corridors efficiently.

articleTitle: Estimation of Lymph Node Metastasis in Cervical Cancer Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Cervical cancer can metastasize to lymph nodes as it progresses. The presence or absence of lymph node metastasis (LNM) is crucial for determining the cancer stage and selecting appropriate treatment methods. However, the diagnostic accuracy of non-invasive imaging for LNM does not match that of biopsy, potentially leading to over- or under-treatment. Therefore, this study aims to develop a method to accurately predict the presence of LNM in cervical cancer, aiding in the determination of appropriate treatment strategies. In this research, we utilize artificial neural network (ANN) and Transformers to predict LNM. Experiments were conducted using 47 metastasis-positive and 95 metastasis-negative cases. The results demonstrated that both the ANN and Transformer models outperformed the 3D CNN (accuracy: 0.817, precision: 0.746, recall: 0.705, F1 score: 0.714), with the Transformer achieving the highest F1 score of 0.867.

articleTitle: Meal Guidance System for Visually Impaired People
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Eating independently is a significant challenge for visually impaired individuals, and meal support devices can help them achieve this goal. Key information such as food types, plate positions, and the amount of remaining food is essential for creating an effective meal support system. This study proposes a method to detect and identify various food types, locate each plate on the dining table, and calculate the remaining food on each plate, expressed as a percentage. The research consists of three main steps. First, we modified the open-source UECFOOD100 dataset, selecting 63 classes of food with 11,140 images for food identification. The YOLO detection model was then trained to identify the food types, while a pre-trained YOLO model was used to detect and locate plates on the table. The bounding boxes generated by the detection model were used to determine the plate positions. Finally, an image processing technique calculated the remaining food on each plate, displaying the value as a percentage. The YOLO algorithm achieved precision, recall, mAP50, and mAP50-95 scores of 0.656, 0.537, 0.596, and 0.425, respectively. The system effectively determines the remaining food percentage on plates, aiding visually impaired individuals in meal management.

articleTitle: Rethinking the Blood Pressure Estimation Modeling Adapted to Cuff Pressure Pulse Waveform Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Hypertension's association with various diseases necessitates daily blood pressure measurement. Although non-invasive devices are high-performing and stable, their portability must be improved from the user's viewpoint. Recently, to increase measurement opportunities, the monitoring situation has changed from the arm to the wrist to a smaller cuff size. This change increases measurement opportunities under conditions where unintended body movements are more likely and lowers the accuracy due to waveform shape variations. Thus, waveform shape variations must be considered despite being ignored in previous studies based on deep learning. To study the model architecture, we performed a contribution analysis of the waveform characteristics of the cuff pressure pulse wave (CPPW), revealing that both local and global features are crucial. Hence, we proposed a novel architecture which has robustness toward waveform shape variations in the CPPW, employing WAVE-U-NET as a feature extractor. Despite the influence of waveform shape variations, we verified that our method showed effective performance especially in SBP compared with other deep-learning-based methods.

articleTitle: Pumping Lemmata for Fuzzy Languages Accepted by Jumping and Right One-Way Jumping Fuzzy Finite Automata
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Jumping finite automata represent an interesting kind of automata working discontinuously over their input. They can read any input symbol and jump without restrictions on any other (not yet processed) symbol. Right one-way jumping finite automata start their reading from the first symbol of the input word, their 'jumps' can be performed only in the left-to-right direction and after reaching the end of the input word, they can resume from its left hand side. This modified specification (in deterministic and nondeterministic variants) leads to automata with different computational power. The paper deals with fuzzy versions of these automata and with pumping lemmata for fuzzy languages accepted by them.

Author Keywords: fuzzy right one-way jumping finite automata
fuzzy nondeterministic right one-way jumping finite automata

articleTitle: Effects of Adversarial Patches Against Object Detection on Combating Cheats in Online First Person Shooter Games
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In FPS (First Person Shooter) games, there exist problematic cheats called “aimbots” that automate a player's (i.e., cheater's) aiming actions at enemies. Such cheats have become a social problem because they cause game companies to lose credibility and users to leave the games. With advances in CV (Computer Vision) technology, CV-based cheat tools for FPS games are becoming pervasive. CV-based cheats are more difficult to be detected than cheats that read in-game memory because they use CV to get enemy's positions. This paper proposes a method to avoid CV-based cheats by applying an adversarial patch to each enemy character, and validates the effects of the proposed method on rate of avoiding YOLOv5-based object detection with respect to loR (Intersection over Recognized object's bounding box) instead of IoU (Intersection over Union) for thresholds of mAP (mean-Average Precision).

articleTitle: Analysis of the Relationship Between Colors and Impression on Studio Ghibli Movie Posters
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: There is a lot of movies in the world, and movie promotion is important to attract consumer attention. The movie poster is one of the most important advertising media among all the movie promotion. There are many related studies focus on the relationship between movie poster colors and people's impressions. However, related studies did not consider the influence of the illustrations and layout of movie posters on the results when a survey was conducted. In this study, we clarify the influence of impressions on only colors used in movie posters by using t-test and factor analysis. The subject posters are six Studio Ghibli movies. The reason is that the opinions of their creators were reflected strongly in the posters, and the Ghibli movies are popular in the world. A survey was conducted by using SD (Semantic Differential) method for revealing the impression of the color chart of movie poster and movie posters. As a result, it was indicated that there was the difference impression between the color chart and the movie poster in five out of the six movies. The results of the experiment show that there is some significance between movie poster colors and impression.

articleTitle: Exploring Individual and Sex Differences from Brain EEG Signals under Music Stimuli
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: The intrinsic mechanisms of how the human brain processes music, a complex and abstract linguistic system, have remained incompletely resolved. Therefore, using experimental data from music-EEG behavioral experiments, the present study proposes a novel large-scale model aimed at dissecting the response of the brain's language system to music stimuli. This study achieved several contributions. First, the significance of gender and individual differences in the data was verified using different nonparametric tests. The results confirmed significant differences in individual responses and gender-related patterns when the human brain was stimulated by music. In addition, the author introduced the idea of visual computing to construct a multimodal model. We finalized the model architecture that was most suitable for parsing human brain EEG signals and music through the ablation study. The baseline model proposed in this study obtained 89.39% accuracy in a binary classification task for sentimental prediction as the downstream task. The significant results obtained by this study are expected to advance the research related to music and human brain activity.

articleTitle: Development of Gait Classification System Using Six-Axis Inertial Sensors by CNN-LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Restoration of walking function is the most important goal of rehabilitation. However, the evaluation of post-stroke rehabilitation lacks quantitative elements. In this study, we used an IMU to acquire the angles of three axes (rotation of x-axis, rotation of y-axis, and rotation of z-axis) of the knee during walking motion as gait parameters. Using this data, machine learning analysis is performed. In this article, we discuss the gait parameters, the angular data of the three axes of the knee, and examine which of the three angular parameters increases or de-creases the generalization ability of the model. As a result, we identify the gait parameters to be used as a dataset. Time series data of the knee angle of one step in the gait measurement was used as the dataset. CNN - LSTM algorithm was used to construct the model. Five subjects were measured with the knee joint motion measurement device attached to both knees. A total of four types of gait movements, including normal gait and three types of gait movements that reproduce hemiplegia, were meas-ured for analysis. Out of one hundred thirty-six steps of data from five subjects, four subjects were used as training data and one unknown subject's data, which was not used during training, was applied to the test data. The results of the prediction of the estimated data show that rotation of z-axis was a parameter that reduced the generalization ability of the model, while rotation of y-axis was a parameter that increased the generalization ability of the model. Prediction results for the rotation of x-axis data alone showed poor accuracy, but when combined with the rotation of y-axis data, the generalization ability was improved.

articleTitle: Tsunami Visualization Tool Using Numerical Simulation Utilizing 3D City Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: After the Noto Peninsula earthquake on January 1, 2024, the importance for residents on the Sea of Japan coast to have a correct understanding of the tsunami hazard is growing. One of the training tools for enhancing tsunami awareness is a tsunami visualization using Virtual Reality (VR). In this study, we create a VR space around Asahi-machi, Sakai-minato City using 3D City Model of PLATEAU, and develop a tsunami evacuation training tool by creating inundation scenarios in the VR space using the results of tsunami inundation simulations with the JAGURS tsunami model.

articleTitle: Generation Z: How Acceptable Health Application for Us?
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Over the course of the last three years, the whole global population has been impacted by a COVID-19 epidemic. As a result of the ongoing pandemic crisis, all human activities have been halted, including remote office work and the closure of crowded locations to further prevent the spread of the virus. The COVID-19 pandemic has led to a significant increase in medical activities, thereby necessitating the employment of digital technology to provide support in managing the situation. One such technology is the Halodoc application, which enables the public to access medical aid without the need for direct contact. This study aims to examine the public's acceptance of the Halodoc application as a result of its usage. The intended participants are those belonging to Generation Z, born between the years 1995 and 2015. Generation Z was selected due to their status as digital natives, meaning they were born into a world where technology is prevalent and constantly evolving. The study utilized the Structural Equation Model (SEM) method to examine the level of acceptance of Generation Z towards the Halodoc application. The Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) was employed as a reference model for this analysis. The analysis will determine whether the model proposed in this study is accepted. This will be done by conducting tests using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) and presenting graphical results from the questionnaire. By doing these tests, it may be determined whether the Halodoc application is deemed acceptable by Generation Z.

articleTitle: A Study of Gender Bias in the Effects of Context Using BERT
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: The corpora used to train large language models contain various social biases. Therefore, various methods have been proposed to investigate the biases contained within language models and to remove biases. In this study, we focus on gender bias and aim to detect gender bias given by contextual information by investigating words within sentences that strongly focus attention on gender words, whereas previous studies have proposed to remove bias by performing direct manipulations on gender words. We create a dataset consisting of pairs of sentences that differ only in male and female words, and use the BERT model to examine the differences in attention values from other words in the sentence to the gender word. Thereby, we will analyze which words provide gender bias within a context. As experimental results, although not conclusive, we observe an overall trend suggesting that there is a correlation between the difference in attention values to gender words and the difference in perplexity of paired sentences containing those words.

articleTitle: LSTM-Based Prediction of Ball Trajectory for Automatic Foul Judgements in Kin-Ball Sport
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Video analysis of sports has become an important means of analyzing the judgment of foul play and performance in matches. Traditionally, most researches have focuses on major sports, but few researches on minor sports have progressed. Therefore, this paper focuses on a minor sport called Kin-Ball and proposes a system for judging fouls in Kin-Ball. One of the fouls in Kin-Ball is called “downward hits,” which is a foul if the trajectory of the ball is not upward at least once from when the ball is hit and to when the ball hits the ground during an attack to the other team. This foul is a feature that does not exist in other sports, and it is very difficult to judge visually by human referees as well, their decision may be ambiguous. Therefore, this paper proposes a novel system for CNN and LSTM-based predicting the trajectory of the ball in Kin-Ball play video taken with a single camera, and automatically judging “downward hits” fouls based on its predicted trajectory.

articleTitle: Toward Fuzzy Reasoning with Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: The objective of this research is to incorporate quantitative inference (especially fuzzy inference) capabilities for real-world environments into large-scale language models. Given the environment and the state of objects when two objects collide, we show that the post-collision state can be inferred in natural language according to this situation. We used T5 to achieve inference with natural language that captures contextual information by using a natural language description of the object's state before the collision as input and the post-collision state as output. The quantitative changes in the physical state of objects are described in vague expressions in natural language sentences, and by simultaneously inferring membership functions corresponding to these vague expressions, it became possible to connect the real world and the language. We also confirmed that the accuracy of inference is improved by dividing the learning steps into multiple steps.

articleTitle: Evolutionary Music Synthesis: A Generative AI System with Interactive User Feedback
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In this study, a music generation system that reflects user preferences by combining music generation AI and inter-active evolutionary computation is proposed. In recent years, the performance of generative AI has been rapidly developing, and it is expected to produce higher quality content. On the other hand, it has not been widely discussed how generative AI can generate music that matches the user's sensibilities. Therefore, this study focuses on interactive evolutionary computation and attempts to generate music that takes user preferences into account by optimizing the input to the generative AI. In this experiment, subjects listen to and evaluate 10 pieces of generated music. The system generates new music based on the user's evaluation. By repeating this process, the music generated by the AI is made closer to the user's intentions. As a result, it was confirmed that approximately 93 % of the subjects felt that the optimized music reflected their own tastes.

articleTitle: Development of a Modular Structured Drone System to Enhance Robotic Functionality
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Recently, the ongoing labor shortage, driven by a declining birthrate and aging population, necessitates more efficient labor solutions. In this context, drones have garnered significant attention due to their high mobility and efficiency, leading to their expanding use in various business applications. However, the capabilities of a single drone are often limited by constraints such as size, power consumption, and thrust, thereby restricting the range of services it can offer. To address these limitations and broaden the scope of drone services, we propose a modular drone system that enables multiple drones to operate collaboratively. This system leverages the strengths of individual drones by allowing them to connect and work together, thereby enhancing overall performance and versatility. The modular approach not only improves scalability but also offers flexibility in configuring drones for specific tasks, ultimately leading to more efficient and effective drone operations. Through this innovative solution, we aim to unlock new possibilities in various industries, including logistics, agriculture, and surveillance through drone system.

articleTitle: Emotional Estimation Method through Fusion of Temporal Skin Temperature and Eye State Changes
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Non-contact facial expression recognition has increased owing to technological advancements and the COVID-19 influence, which is vital for assessing digital content interest and quality. Studies demonstrate that changes in facial skin temperature, particularly in the nose and cheek areas, can be used for emotion estimation, with thermal images outperforming visible images. However, research on time-series data and the integration of thermal and visible images remains limited. In this study, we propose a method for estimating strong emotional arousal during digital content viewing using time-series data from thermal and visible images. Consequently, we achieved an estimation accuracy of over 80% by combining changes in facial skin temperature and the eyes opening degree.

articleTitle: Optimizing Job Shop Scheduling with Deep Q-Network for Robust Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In recent years, with the emergence of new technologies such as smart manufacturing and smart factories, establishing effective and robust scheduling systems has become an important issue. The job shop scheduling problem (JSP) is a typical scheduling problem that involves scheduling work orders under constraints such as order sequence and designated machines. Addressing the JSP using heuristic rules or meta-heuristics can yield good scheduling results. However, it is difficult for these scheduling methods to adapt to a dynamic manufacturing environment, requiring rescheduling to replan orders. This study uses deep reinforcement learning as the scheduling model to address this issue. In the proposed method, we use deep Q-Network to optimize JSP. By designing a novel reward function, the model can maintain relatively stable scheduling results without rescheduling. The experimental results show that the model used in this study achieves more robust scheduling results compared with other scheduling methods under uncertain environmental factors.

articleTitle: Crack Detection and 3D Scene Creation of Road Bridge Using Deep Learning and Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In Japan, the number of social infrastructure facilities, such as bridges and tunnels, which were constructed during a period of high economic growth and have been in existence for 50 years, has been increasing, and inspection is important for managing them. In 2014, it became obligatory to inspect structures once every 5 years. From the above decision, the inspection of structures by engineers using close-up visual observation and visible light images has been carried out periodically. However, damage inspection by visual inspection has become a problem from the viewpoint of cost such as human cost, the viewpoint of labor, and time cost. The periodical inspection is determined to utilize close-up visual observation by engineers or the equivalent diagnosis, and digitization and sharing of the inspection results are important in the management of infrastructure. Therefore, the construction of a system that carries out the diagnosis equivalent to close-up visual observation and digitizes the result is tried.

articleTitle: User-Adaptive Chat Dialogue System Based on User's Feedback
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: We develop a chat dialogue system that responds according to the preferences of each user, aiming to improve user satisfaction when interacting with the system. This system receives explicit feedbacks from the user on whether or not the user prefers each response of the system during the dialogue, and thus it recognizes the user's preference regarding the style of response such as dialogue acts and politeness. The system generates multiple candidate response sentences using a deep learning model T5 and selects the one that best matches the user's preference. In this way, our dialogue system responds according to the user's preference. The result of an evaluation experiment shows that the proposed system generates responses that match the user's preferences better than a system that does not take user's preferences into account.

articleTitle: DDTNet: A Dense Network with Dendritic Learning for Brain Tumor Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence has transformed the field of medical image analysis, particularly in the detection of brain tumors. The implementation of deep learning techniques has significantly enhanced the precision of tumor localization and size estimation, thereby improving the accuracy of tumor identification and pre-diagnosis. However, existing methods often suffer from poor edge detection, leading to the poor classification performance due to weak nonlinear feature representations. To alleviate this problem, we propose a novel architecture termed Dendritic Dense Tumor-detection Network (DDTNet). This architecture introduces dendritic neuron module to enhance nonlinear feature representation at the end of dense networks. By leveraging the superior non-linear capabilities of DNMs to emulate dendritic neuron behavior, DDTNet facilitates improved feature classification. Experimental results on publicly available datasets demonstrate that DDTNet outperforms both traditional DenseNet and other state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy and computational efficiency. For the brain tumor detection classification problem, our model achieves an accuracy of 96.3 % and an F1 score of 96.2 %. This study suggests that utilizing DNM as classifiers could facilitate the development of more effective deep learning models for classification tasks.

articleTitle: Prediction of Cardiovascular Disease Development for CEA Patients Using Multimodal Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Carotid endarterectomy (CEA) is a surgical treatment for carotid artery stenosis for stroke prevention. Although CEA has been shown to be effective in patients with severe plaque stenosis, predicting long-term outcomes after CEA re-mains difficult. There are many studies that predict prognosis using patients' clinical data, but there are no studies that predict prognosis using carotid plaque pathological images. This study aims to predict the development of cardiovascular disease within one year after surgery in patients undergoing CEA using multimodal learning that combines carotid plaque pathological images, patient's clinical data, and pathologists' interpretation. Moreover, the proposed method contributes to detecting pathological factors and clinical features associated with the development of cardiovascular disease. Pathological risk scores obtained by the anomaly detection model were combined with clinical information and textual features obtained by TF-IDF and they are classified by XGBoost, resulting in a ROC-AUC of 0.850 and a PR-AUC of 0.816. These values showed better classification performance than when each feature was used alone.

articleTitle: Automated Detection and Classification of Mandibular Third Molar Impactions in Panoramic X-Rays
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Mandibular third molar impaction is a common clinical issue requiring high diagnostic accuracy and efficiency due to potential complications such as infections, pain, and adj acent tooth damage. Traditional manual diagnosis is time-consuming and reliant on clinical experience, increasing the risk of misdiagnosis. To address this challenge, this paper introduces an advanced method utilizing the YOLOv7 algorithm for automatic detection and classification of mandibular third molar impactions based on Winter's classification in panoramic X-rays. Leveraging a dataset of 450 images annotated to include both second and third molars, two distinct approaches are proposed. The first approach detects and classifies both second and third molars within a single bounding box, while the second approach focuses solely on the third molar. The results showed mean average precision (mAP) scores of 0.5820 for the first approach and 0.7226 for the second approach, with a total of 10 classes (five classes on each side of the image). This method demonstrates significant potential for improving diagnostic accuracy and efficiency in dental radiography.

articleTitle: Investigating Global Search Performance of Multi-Objective Genetic Algorithm based on Innately Split Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel search method that apply the global recursive dividing strategy of DIRECT to the recursive initialization strategy of ISM. It is a frame-work that runs Genetic Algorithm multiply for multi-objective optimization. Additionally, we create two benchmark problems of multi-objective NK model and investigate the global search performance of our method by them. Experimental results show that our method outperforms the baseline in terms of the global search performance of the design variable space.

articleTitle: Investigation of Finger Motion and Brain Activity in a Novel Human Grasping Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This study investigated the utility of a human grasping algorithm based on finger motion and brain activity to understand how humans determine finger postures to properly grasp an object. A grasping experiment was conducted to measure finger motion and brain activity while thirteen participants grasped cylinders. Finger motion was captured using an optical motion capture system, using the coordinates of reflective markers attached to the participants' hands. Finger joint angles were calculated from the marker coordinates, and were used to reveal the order in which joint postures are determined for grasping. Brain activity was measured using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) to measure hemodynamic changes. Gradients of these fNIRS signals were analyzed to explore changes in brain activity while grasping postures were determined. The grasping motion differed among individuals, indicating that finger postures for grasping were determined in different orders. Specifically, some participants determined their grasping postures without showing significant temporal differences between each joint, while others did not. The latter group was further divided into those who determined the postures of the distal or proximal joints first and those who determined the posture of the thumb first. The fNIRS signals during grasping varied according to the grasping process. When participants grasped cylinders without modifying their grasping posture, the gradients of the fNIRS signals tended to be highest after completion of the grasping. Conversely, when participants were permitted to modify their grasping posture for the best posture, the gradients tended to be highest during the grasping and then decreased. These results may help us to understand the grasping algorithm and apply this algorithm to grasping simulations, robot hands, and prosthetic hands.

articleTitle: Sound Source Separation of Japanese Tree Frog (Hyla Japonica) and Black-Spotted Pond Frog (Pelophylax Nigromaculatus)
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In this study, we aim to develop a bioacoustics-based monitoring system for non-native species such as the Tokyo daruma pond frog (Pelophylax porous porous) in Hokkaido. We created a sound source separation model based on “Cocktail Party Source Separation” to separate frog calls from mixed audio recordings. A neural network model was trained using data from the Japanese tree frogs (Hyla japonica) and Black-spotted pond frogs (Pelophylax nigromaculatus) to separate mixed frog calls. The evaluation results showed successful separation with some issues in frequency-range after source separation. Future improvements are required to refine the model by incorporating multi-channel data for better separation quality to improve the performance of species identification and sound source estimation.

articleTitle: Utilization of Genre Information in Collaborative Filtering by Three-mode Fuzzy Co-Clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Recommendation ability of collaborative filtering (CF) is expected to be improved by utilizing not only user-item cooccurrence information but also additional information. In this paper, co-clustering-based CF is improved by introducing three-mode fuzzy co-clustering, where user-item cooccurrence information is utilized in conjunction with additional genre information on each item. User-item co-clusters are extracted such that users' preference tendencies on items are summarized by considering their intrinsic preferences on genre categories, and then, the recommendation capability of co-clustering-based CF can be improved even with sparse cooccurrence information. Experimental results with MovieLens benchmark data demon-strate that recommendation performance is improved by properly increasing the responsibility degree of genre information.

articleTitle: Virtual Agent Driven Peer Learning System to Enhance Exercise Motivation
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In this study, we propose a system that leverages peer learning to enhance exercise motivation by facilitating mutual instruction and feedback between users and conversational agents on exercise performance. The system aims to address the challenge of maintaining motivation for continuous exercise, which is recommended for preventing lifestyle-related diseases that have become an increasing health concern. The proposed system implements a peer learning environment where the user and agent take turns acting as an exercise buddy - performing exercises and offering advice to improve each other's form. Over 80 % of participants reported enjoying exercising more with this reciprocal system compared to one with unilateral instruction from the agent. These findings suggest peer learning between users and conversational agents could effectively boost motivation for exercise.

articleTitle: Observer Design for Takagi-Sugeno Fuzzy Descriptor System Using a Lyapunov Function with Integrals of the Membership Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: We discuss an observer design for nonlinear descriptor systems described by Takagi-Sugeno fuzzy descriptor system, which can represent a broader class of systems, including not only differential equations but also algebraic equations, compared to the standard Takagi-Sugeno fuzzy system. The observer design is important to estimate the state of systems because not all states of systems can be measured in many cases. In this paper, we propose a new observer based on a descriptor form and a Lyapunov function candidate structured using integrals of the membership functions to obtain a relaxed observer design condition. Finally, a numerical example is shown to illustrate the comparison of our observer design methods and others based on the conventional Lyapunov functions.

articleTitle: Development Reading System and Detection of Lesion Candidate in Capsule Endoscopy Using YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: An endoscopy capsule is a device with a diameter of approximately 11 mm and a length of approximately 26 mm; it is ingested to capture images within the gastrointestinal tract. Compared with conventional endoscopy, capsule endoscopy places a lesser burden on patients and enables the observation of the small intestine.
