This noninvasive technique generates more than 50,000 images in a single examination. Because of the necessity for physicians to visually inspect each image, the diagnostic process is time-consuming and labor-intensive. This study is to create a user interface that presents lesion candidates and diagnostically inconclusive images with the aim of reducing the burden on physicians, preventing missed lesions, and assisting physicians in diagnosis. The lesion candidates and diagnostically inconclusive images are detected by deep learning. In addition, to support diagnosis, we implemented functions such as speed adjustment, number of images, luminance correction, and 4 modes to limit the images to be displayed. An evaluation test of the created user interface prototype was conducted. The evaluation results showed that the average score exceeded 4 points on 4 of the 7 axes, confirming its effectiveness. The 3 axes that scored below the average of 4 points revealed areas for improvement, such as designing with movement and change, and adding explanations using tooltips. Those changes resulted in an average score of 4 or higher on 6 of the 7 axes, confirming the improvement.

articleTitle: Food image classification based on the Swin Transformer model
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Food classification is an important task in computer vision applications ranging from dietary assessment to food recognition on social media. In this study, we propose a food image classification technique utilizing the Swin Transformer, a transformer-based architecture. modern transformer architectures like the Swin Transformer capture long-range dependencies within images, making them suitable for complex visual recognition tasks. The primary objective of this study was to evaluate the performance of the Swin Transformer in food classification tasks and compare it with existing CNN-based models, such as MobileNet, and other transformer-based models like Vision Transformer. The experimental results demonstrate that the Swin Transformer effectively handles intricate relationships in food images, achieving high classification accuracy.

articleTitle: Global Path Planning Based on Rough Terrain Perception Using Growing Neural Gas
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: The development of autonomous mobile robots has been a persistent challenge, and their application in outdoor, rough terrain environments is especially beneficial. We propose a traversability perception method based on Growing Neural Gas with Different Topologise in the unknown rough terrain. Next, we propose a path planning method that utilizes the result of the traersability estimation. Finally, we conduct an experiment in a real environment to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Constrained Multi-Modal Multi-Objective Evolutionary Algorithm with Problem Transformation into Two-Objective Subproblems
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Real-world optimization problems often have multi-ple conflicting objective functions to be optimized simultaneously. In some of them, there are different Pareto optimal solutions with the same objective function values. Those problems are called multi-modal multi-objective optimization problems (MMOPs). For MMOPs, we proposed a decomposition-based multi-modal multi-objective evolutionary algorithm called MM2T in our previous study. However, MM2T does not consider constraints and thus cannot solve constrained MMOPs (CMMOPs). To apply MM2T to CMMOPs, we introduce the constrained dominance principle (CDP) into MM2T. We examine the search performance of MM2T with CDP through computational experiments.

articleTitle: Generating Adversarial Examples for 3D Point Clouds Using Evolutionary Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: We propose a general attack framework based on evolutionary algorithms to quickly and efficiently generate low-perturbation adversarial samples for 3D point cloud data. Specifically, we employ a random selection to increase or decrease the number of points perturbed, followed by a single-objective evolutionary algorithm to adjust the magnitude of the perturbations. Additionally, we design an extended version that introduces a multi-objective optimization algorithm to simultaneously optimize the magnitude of the perturbations and attack effectiveness. To evaluate the performance of the proposal, we compare it with other classic algorithms using the ModelNet40 dataset. Experimental results show that the attack algorithm based on evolutionary algorithms can successfully fool well-trained models with acceptable perturbations and a higher success rate.

articleTitle: Preliminary Analysis of Impression Changes by Adding a Pause to Piece Movement Motions of an Arm Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In this study, we aim to design movements for game-playing arm robots, such as those used in chess and shogi, to convey the player's internal state through the way the robot moves the game pieces. Toward this goal, we analyze how different movement styles affect impressions of the robot arm. In Experiment 1, we examine how impressions vary depending on the presence and location of pauses in the arm's movements. In Experiment 2, we investigate how pauses in response to the opponent's (participant's) hand motion influence perceptions of the robot. The experimental results showed that the existence of the pause can change the robot's impressions.

articleTitle: Deep Convolutional Learning-Based Unit Action Recognition for Analyzing Skilled Worker Behavior
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This paper aims to standardize the actions of skilled workers and recognize them using the R2plus1D algorithm. The process videos were defined by 10-unit actions, and training was conducted using the R2plus1D algorithm. To address the issue of decreased recognition accuracy at segments where unit actions change, the concepts of ‘margin’ and the sliding window technique were introduced.

articleTitle: Extension of Fuzzy c-Lines Considering Compactness and Separation of Clusters
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Fuzzy c-Means (FCM)-type clustering is designed for finding compact clusters but sometime fails to distinguish adjacent clusters due to overlapping characteristics at local minima. Fuzzy Compactness and Separation (FCS) is an extension of FCM, which is designed for finding compact but separate clusters by using the combined objective function of the FCM aggregation criterion and the cluster separation measure. In this paper, FCS is further extended to linear fuzzy clustering, where the FCM prototypes are replaced with lines. Although Fuzzy c-Lines (FCL) uses the clustering criterion of distances among each data point and prototypical lines, the degree of cluster distortion is also measured by the distances among each data object and the global centroid in conjunction with distortions on each linear prototype. Experimental results demonstrate that the initialization sensitivity can be improved by introducing the separation criterion in linear fuzzy clustering.

articleTitle: Analysis of Relationships Between Gaze and Body Movements Toward Searching State Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: The demand for communication robots has been increasing due to a shortage of human resources. These robots need to estimate human internal states, such as their interests or intentions. In this study, we focus on two internal states: searching and non-searching. We analyze the differences in the relationships between gaze, head, and body movements in these states. To achieve this, we created a VR experimental environment with two task types: search and non-search tasks. Participants were instructed to perform these tasks in the VR environment while their motion data was recorded and analyzed. The results showed that the relationships between gaze and body movements differ between the search and non-search tasks.

articleTitle: Extracting Motion Patterns of Greeting Gestures Using GNG with Spiking Neuron Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This study focuses on behavior patterns, which are characteristic actions common to groups or communities, to promote intercultural understanding. Understanding greeting gestures is crucial for comprehending social relationships, but these vary across cultures and regions. Recent advancements in sensing technology and artificial intelligence, such as RGB-D cameras and markerless motion capture systems, have made it easier to capture motion data in diverse formats. Therefore, it is important to extract relevant motion patterns and apply appropriate structuring for effective long-term archiving. We propose a method for extracting motion patterns using a Growing Neural Gas (GNG) algorithm with a Spiking Neuron Model. Additionally, this paper presents an experimental example of extracting a gesture pattern in Indonesian style.

articleTitle: A Decomposition-based Constrained Multi-objective Evolutionary Algorithm with Adaptive Weight Adjustment
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Many real-world optimization problems have multi-ple conflicting objectives and constraints to be considered simultaneously. These problems are referred to as constrained multi-objective optimization problems (CMOPs). To handle CMOPs, constrained multi-objective evolutionary algorithms (CMOEAs) have been proposed so far, including CMOEA with problem transformation from a CMOP to two-objective problems (CM2T). CM2T decomposes a CMOP into a set of two-objective subprob-lems using uniformly distributed weight vectors. In general, the uniformity of weight vectors can improve the solution diversity along the Pareto front (PF). However, it cannot work well when the PF is disconnected or is composed of feasible and infeasible regions. This paper incorporates an adaptive weight vector adjustment mechanism into CM2T (CM2T-AWA). We compare CM2T-AWA with six state-of-the-art CMOEAs on two constrained test suites. The experimental results shows that the proposed algorithm is superior to the comparison algorithms.

articleTitle: A Study on Brain Decoding of Image Stimuli Using a Diffusion Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Humans recognize the external world by processing information received by the eyes and other sensory organs in the brain. Understanding how the human brain processes complex information from the outside world is expected to improve the performance of image and speech recognition technologies, which have made remarkable progress in recent years. In this study, we focus on brain activity decoding of visual experience, aim to read what humans are looking at by predicting image features from brain activity data, and further attempt to develop a method to output high-definition and semantically valid images by generating images from predicted features using a diffusion model. As a result, similarity to the stimulus image was confirmed in the image generated by the training data, but the evaluation data confirmed that there is still room for further study.

articleTitle: Building a Role-Play Interactive System using LLM for Health Guidance Education
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This study develops a “health guidance training system for nursing students” using conversational AI to simulate patient interactions. Health guidance aims to understand health states and change unhealthy behaviors to prevent lifestyle-related diseases, often employing role-playing as a training method. However, traditional role-playing suffers from student's shyness and inexperience. Our solution leverages the ChatVRM system, which integrates speech recognition, natural language generation, speech synthesis, and 3D avatars to create a simulated patient. The system was evaluated by nursing students and faculty through our surveys, with over 70% of participants providing positive feedback on its usefulness, ease of use, and natural interaction. These results suggest the system effectively enhances health guidance training by providing realistic and practical simulations. In future work, we will further improve the system and conduct extensive evaluation experiments.

articleTitle: Neural Network Modeling and PID Control for 3- DOF Horizontal Stabilization Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This paper proposes a method to implement an 3-dof stabilization device by combining a neural network with a PID controller. First, hardware was designed based on the Inverted Delta Robot structure. This platform, equipped with three servo motors and an IMU sensor, is suggested as a real-time stabilization platform. Second, using servo motors with limited angular movement, real-time data on Roll and Pitch angles were collected. Third, the collected data were preprocessed, and a neural network model with the ReLU function as the activation function was trained. Fourth, the trained model was used to output stabilization error values to the PID controller, maintaining the device's balance. This study demonstrates the potential of combining neural networks with PID controllers for stabilization devices. Future research will require experiments in various industrial environments, sensor integration, and neural network optimization.

articleTitle: Facial Video Analysis using Eye-tracking data during Japanese Text Reading
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This study aims to develop a system capable of discerning the emotions of text reader through their facial expression and eye movement. The research explores effective combinations of facial video image and eye movement using four machine learning models. The findings highlight the value of integrating eye movement data in facial image analysis. The method achieved a notable detection accuracy of 0.7338 for identifying facial expressions of confusion during silent text reading.

articleTitle: An Identification System for Sperm Whales (Physeter Macrocephalus) Based on Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This paper proposes an identification system for sperm whales (Physeter macrocephalus) using images of their flukes as input to the system. The proposed system consists of two parts: one part extracts the region of the fluke to be identified from the images taken by a digital camera, The other part identifies the whale from its fluke image. Deep learning methods called deeplabv3 and CascadePSPNet are used to extract the fluke area from the input image, and metric learning using the Adacos loss function constructs an identification model. Experimental results show that high identification accuracies (top-I and top-5 accuracies) are achieved by the proposed system.

articleTitle: On a New Rough Clustering Based on Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to develop and investigate a new rough clustering based on optimization. We propose a restructured algorithm using only one variable, instead of the algorithm described using two variables in existing methods. We also perform numerical examples using artificial data and the Iris and Wine datasets. This research has the potential to be used as a method for determining false negatives and false positives in cancer diagnosis.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison Between RC-OFDM and PORC-OFDM in Visible Light Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Visible Light Communication (VLC) is a new communication method that uses the high-speed response of semi-conductor devices such as light-emitting diodes and photodiodes, and has the advantages of high-speed communication, high security level, and high energy efficiency compared to radio wave communication. However, the degradation of transmission quality due to background optical noise is an issue. One solution against this problem is to apply the OFDM to the VLC to block the frequency band of background optical noise. There is also the RC-OFDM, which improves communication quality by repeated transmission, but it has the disadvantage of decreasing transmission efficiency. As a countermeasure, the authors have proposed the PORC-OFDM, which suppresses the decline in transmission efficiency by adding a phase offset according to the additional information bits during repeated transmission. In this study, the effectiveness of applying the PORC-OFDM to the VLC systems is experimentally verified by the comparison with the conventional RC-OFDM.

articleTitle: Faster Algorithms for a Lexicographic Bi-Criteria Line Balancing Problem with Totally Ordered Precedence Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: The line balancing has been an important production strategy which aims at redressing the balance of workloads on machines in an assembly type of production system. In this paper, a lexicographic bi-criteria optimization model of the line balancing is revisited for a mass-production of one homogeneous product. A sequence of machines and a totally ordered set of tasks are given. The machines are considered to be situated along with a production line, according to their sequence. Precedence relations between tasks are specified by the total order of tasks. The task set also consists of a given number of disjoint subsets, namely categories such that tasks in a category are considered to constitute a certain kind of family of technical skills. Each task has a positive processing time and a category index. A solution to the problem is expressed by an assignment of tasks to machines, and for the feasibility of a solution, the assignment must obey the totally ordered precedence constraint on tasks. The sum of processing times of tasks assigned to a machine in a feasible solution is the load of the machine, and the number of category indexes of tasks assigned to a machine is referred to as the degree of diverseness of the task subset. The primary objective of the problem is to minimize the maximum machine load, and the second objective is to minimize the maximum degree of diverseness of tasks assigned to a machine. The lexicographic bi-criteria line balancing problem with totally ordered precedence constraints has been known to admit a polynomial time exact algorithm, whose time complexity is linear in the number of machines and squared in the number of tasks. In this paper, a faster polynomial time exact algorithm is proposed, which improves the time complexity to be squared in the number of tasks.

articleTitle: In Vitro Experiments and Computational Modeling of Cancer Invasion
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Understanding cancer invasion dynamics is crucial for developing effective treatments and therapies. This paper first reports the results of our cancer invasion experiments, demonstrating that two different breast cancer cell lines, MCF7 and T-47D, exhibit distinct invasion patterns. To understand the mechanisms underlying these patterns, we then develop a computational model using the Cellular Potts model. This model accounts for cell-cell adhesion, membrane protrusion, and contact inhibition of proliferation. Simulation results based on the model show that it is able to reproduce the invasion patterns observed in experiments. Additionally, the simulation results indicate that cell-cell adhesion plays an important role in determining the invasion patterns of cancer cells.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence for the “INSIDER”
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: “INSIDER” is a communication game. This game shares similarities with “Werewolf” and “Twenty Questions,” but it is characterized by the need to steer the conversation in a way that conceals one's role from others. The detail of game's rule is explained in the second chapter. The goal of this paper is to describe building a human-like AI agent that plays the “INSIDER”. This game is conversational game with some players to figure out the secret topic. The AI agent is required to think inductively and deductively to find out the secret topic and the Insider player. So, it is necessary for the agent to have quantified knowledge and to make decisions with the knowledge. All of the knowledge that the AI agent has is represented in a table. And it must narrow down topic candidates with questions. Information entropy is the best indicator to observe the communication games. Because everything can be a topic candidate. And all information about topic is accounted for with or without possession. It is important to vectorize the flow of conversation and to represent the distance between two concepts in the ontology. Information entropy makes it possible to quantify the distance. For the first step, we built an AI agent that uses information entropy to deduce the topic using a deductive approach. This approach is different depending on the role. Then, we let the AI agents play the “INSIDER” and observed the game log and transition of information entropy. Then the content of knowledge given to the AI agents in each experiment is changed, and differences in the outcome are recorded in the game log.

articleTitle: Application Of Deep Learning To Basic Surveys For Setting Steep Slope Warning Areas
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This study uses a deep learning technique to output the slope failure warning areas from numerical elevation data. This is treated as a semantic segmentation task, with U-Net as the network model. The experiment results are compared for cases in which the loss function is used and in which other modifications are made to incorporate the idea of disaster countermeasures.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Effects on Driving Behaviors due to Changes in Engine Sound Feedback
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Despite ongoing advancements in driving assistance systems, the risk of traffic accidents remains. This study explores how altering engine sound feedback can influence speed adjustment, mainly through accelerator control, without directly changing the vehicle's behavior or alerting the driver. Our experiments using a VR-based driving simulator show that this method can potentially modify driving behavior.

articleTitle: Detection System for Automotive Engine Governor Based on CNN Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This study develops an automated defect detection system based on a CNN (Convolutional Neural Network) for rapid governor rotation and evaluates its performance. In the proposed paper, the governor is used in diesel engines to regulate fuel injection amounts to maintain the engine's rotational speed consistently. The governor is rotated using a servo motor at speeds of 700rpm, 1000rpm, 2000rpm, 2800rpm, and 3200rpm, and the degree of opening of the governor is captured using a camera. A CNN is employed to detect defect states using the captured images of the governor's opening degree. Experimental results evaluate the performance using the CNN algorithm Inception. This study demonstrates the application of CNN-based models to improve defect detection systems in manufacturing processes.

articleTitle: Snuggling Robot at Different Positions Based on User's Facial Expressions
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This study proposes a pet robot designed to enhance emotional interaction with users by adapting its behavior based on the recognition of facial expressions. The proposed system enables the robot to interpret a user's smile as an invitation to approach directly, while a sad expression prompts it to move closer in a comforting manner. Interaction results indicated that the robot's movement away from the user elicited feelings of loneliness and discomfort, whereas movements toward the user, alongside gentle snuggling and rotational gestures, fostered a sense of familiarity and reassurance.

articleTitle: Beamspace AIC & MDL Algorithm for Based on Concentric Circular Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In modern wireless communication systems using multiple antenna elements, accurately identifying the signals contained in the received signal is very important. Conventional signal number estimation algorithms operate for the entire set of antenna elements, resulting in high computational complexity. In order to enhance this high computational complexity problem, this paper proposes beamspace based Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) and Minimum Description Length (MDL) algorithms based on a concentric circular array (CCA) antenna for efficient signal number estimation. In addition, computer simulation results are presented to evaluate the signal-number estimation performance of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Damage Assessment of Concrete Beams Based on Fractal Analysis and Drift
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Assessment of damage state of concrete structures after earthquakes is often based on the human empirical visual inspection. Crack distribution, referred to as crack pattern, is a common damage assessment index along with crack width and drift ratio. Fractal analysis has been used to quantify the crack pattern on the surface of concrete components. This paper focuses on the quantification of crack patterns through image analysis and aims to develop an assessment model in the form of a relationship between fractal dimension and transient drift for concrete beams. A total of eleven concrete beams were tested under half-cyclic loading to investigate the usefulness of fractal analysis in damage assessment for concrete beams, and the test results are used to calibrate the proposed model. The box-counting algorithm is adopted for the fractal analysis in this study. The test results reveal that fractal dimension is an efficient image-based indicator of damage degree of concrete beams and correlates strongly with the drift and aspect ratio of the beams. To verify efficiency of quantitative assessment based on fractal dimension, the correlation between fractal dimension and relative stiffness loss, an overall damage index measuring both external and internal damage, are examined.

articleTitle: Study of Chromatograph Parts Using a 3D Printer and Separation Motion Trajectories
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: The three axes, the solar axis (angular velocity (ω1), planetary axis (ω2), and satellite axis (ω3), rotate so that the sum of ω2 and ω3 is ω1. Next, the J-type high-speed countercurrent chromatograph system rotates the solar axis and planetary axis so that ω1 and ω2 are the same. The trajectories of the rotational motion and the acceleration at the time of separation in these cases are derived and compared. Furthermore, the MPS method (Moving Particle Semi-Implicit method) is used for fluid analysis to evaluate the degree of separation due to the motion.

articleTitle: DFedMD: Decentralized Federated Learning using Model Distillation
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Conventional machine learning methods require devices to transfer their data to a central server because the server intensively stores all the data and trains the model. However, if the data are sensitive or large in volume, sending them may cause problems in terms of privacy and network bandwidth consumption. To address these problems, federated learning (FL), in which data are distributed across devices without being aggregated into a server, has garnered attention. Moreover, decentralized FL (DFL) is a serverless learning method that improves the accuracy of each client model by exchanging information necessary for model learning with neighboring clients in a distributed network to which the clients are directly connected. In this study, we propose a novel method of DFL that maintains data and model secrecy through knowledge distillation. To use knowledge distillation effectively, we utilize a data-free model distillation using mismatch data. Furthermore, to avoid rapid accuracy degradation during training, the knowledge loss function in the proposed method incorporates the output of its initial model into error calculations. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method improves accuracy compared with the case in which each client learns using only their own data.

articleTitle: Some Variants of Fuzzy $c$-Directions Clustering Algorithms for Spherical Data
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Fuzzy c-means (FCM) is the most fundamental fuzzy clustering algorithm for vectorial data, and several variants have been proposed, including the q-divergence based FCM, Yang-type FCM, and extended q-divergence-based FCM. However, only the Yang-type fuzzification technique has been applied to fuzzy c-directions (FCD) clustering for spherical data. In this regard, two fuzzy clustering algorithms were investigated for fuzzy c-directions. The two algorithms are q-divergence based FCD and extended q-divergence-based FCD, which are constructed by replacing the object-cluster dissimilarity used in the q -divergence- based FCM and extended q -divergence- based FCM respectively, with that in the FCD for spherical data. Based on numerical experiments with an artificial data set, the characteristics of each method are presented. The characteristics of each method are presented based on numerical experiments using an artificial dataset.

articleTitle: The Combined Localization Based on TDOA and FDOA for High-Speed Moving Object
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Detecting the location of high-speed moving objects is a critical issue in various fields including the medical, emergence service, aerospace, defense areas, etc. In general, Time Difference of Arrival (TDOA) and Frequency Difference of Arrival (FDOA) techniques are primarily used for estimating the location of a moving object. Although these techniques provide excellent estimation performance for the stationary or low speed moving object, they may have significant location estimation errors for the high-speed object moving. In order to improve this problem, this paper introduces the combined localization method based on TDOA and FDOA for estimating the location of high-speed moving objects efficiently.

articleTitle: Threshold-Free Event Detection for Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring Using Recurrence Plot and Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Event detection is a crucial process in Non-intrusive Load Monitoring(NILM). Correct detection results not only can improve the accuracy of subsequent load identification but also quickly understand the real-time status of the system, so as to maintain the stability of power supply and the security of power dispatching. In the process of electricity consumption, the change of the switching state may cause an electrical appliance to be cut off or started, which is regarded as an event in the load identification process. However, after actual measurement, it is found that in the start process of the switch, some existing household appliances may produce a large surge when starting, while some may produce only a small one. Therefore, if the method of setting the threshold is adopted to determine whether an event has occurred, it will be difficult to obtain the appropriate threshold. For this reason, in this paper, a new feature is proposed to determine whether an event has occurred. This feature is that when the root-mean-square(RMS) current is converted to Recurrence PLOT(RP), the RP will present a geometry in different colors, so that there will be a clear distinction between events and non-events. Therefore, if such images are used to train Convolution Neural Network(CNN), events and non-events can be classified in a way without threshold configuration, and event detection can be completed. In this study, two public data sets were used to verify the suitability of the method. As shown by experimental data, the proposed method can achieve an identification rate of 98%”,99%, indicating that this method is better than other existing methods.

articleTitle: An Analysis of Patellar Movement and Posture During Stepping Using RGB-D Cameras and Inertial Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Patellar tracking can be measured to more effectively evaluate and treat joint disorders, but noninvasive and dynamic measurement is difficult. Therefore, the final goal of this study is to analyze and diagnose the patella during gait, and as a pilot study, develop a system to noninvasively and quantitatively evaluate patellar movement and posture during stepping. A measurement system using four depth cameras is used to acquire point cloud data of the knee joint shape. The system performs an axial basis transformation of the point cloud data using the positions of green markers attached to both ends of the knee and the angle of the thigh acquired by inertial sensors. This process enables analysis of three-dimensional knee motions such as stepping. The patella shape point cloud is detected by 3D registration, and the amount of movement and posture are analyzed. In this experiment, we analyzed the patellar movement and posture of three healthy subjects while stepping on their feet. The highly accurate analysis results showed that the patella moved medially during knee flexion and then laterally during knee flexion. It was also confirmed that the patella is flexed sagittally with knee flexion and tilts laterally when the knee flexion exceeds 20 degrees. However, due to noise in the point cloud data, reproducibility could not be obtained for all subjects. By solving the problem and developing the current system to measure and analyze patellar tracking during gait, it may be possible to perform postoperative evaluation of patellar tracking during gait for patients with patellar dislocation symptoms.

articleTitle: Analysis of Placental Oxygenation in BOLD MRI for Fetal Growth Restriction Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Fetal Growth Restriction (FGR) is an obstetric and gynecological disease, resulting in low fetal weight at gestational age. It causes fetal growth delay during gestation and increases the risk of prenatal and postnatal health problems. Recently, some studies have reported that fetal growth is related to placental oxygenation that can be visualized using BOLD MRI. The BOLD MRI image analysis using machine learning requires the placental region mask, but its manual annotation requires a heavy burden on experts. In this paper, we apply image registration in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\mathrm{D}+\mathrm{t}$</tex> images to reduce the annotation workload from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\mathrm{D}+\mathrm{t}$</tex> times to one time, and extract statistical image features in the auto-annotated placental regions to validate the image features related to the clinical data of FGR and non-FGR patients. The experiment on BOLD MRI of 8 FGR and 15 non-FGR patients showed that the proposed method recognized the placental region in dice coefficient of 0.779. Experiments using the extracted feature analysis found the correlation to the clinical data in placental weight and fetal birth weight. From these results, the proposed method is expected to be used for the evaluation of placental oxygenation and FGR diagnosis.

articleTitle: Estimation of Presence or Absence of Learning Understanding Using EEG and ECG Based on CNN Models
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a method to estimate the presence or absence of learning understanding by combining electroencephalogram (EEG) and electrocardiogram (ECG). The proposed method employs convolutional neural network (CNN) models to extract features for classifying the presence or absence of understanding. Each CNN model is to extract the features of EEG and ECG, and combine the extracted EEG and ECG features. To show the effectiveness of the proposed method, we conducted experiments using real EEG and ECG data. The experimental results showed higher discrimination accuracy using the proposed method compared with the methods using EEG or ECG.

articleTitle: Movement Classification Method for Awake Bruxism Using sEMG Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This paper presents a method to classify five brux-ism movements and three daily movements using surface elec-tromyographic (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex>EMG) signals obtained from the left and right masseter muscles, which are the muscles in the cheek. Forty features, eight window sizes for extracting features from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex>EMG signals, and eight classifiers were evaluated to design a suitable classification method. As a result, the highest classification accuracy of 96.57% was achieved by using a Support Vector Machine with the following eight features: MSR, LD, MYOP, SSC, MEAN, AAC, AR, and MMAV2, extracted with a window of 0.75 [<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex>] at a sampling rate of 2000 [Hz] and an analog-digital conversion resolution of 10 [bit].

articleTitle: Analysis and Identification of Gait Balance States using Plantar Pressure Distribution
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Among the various forms of accidents that occur in construction work, crashes and falls account for the largest percentage. In this study, we attempted to identify the balance state during walking from the measured plantar pressure data that were measured the changes in plantar pressure during balanced and unbalanced walking condition using plantar pressure sensors. Specifically, we proposed a method to convert plantar pressure data during linear walking under three different walking conditions into a feature vector during a walking cycle. Furthermore, we proposed a method to identify three types of walking conditions using a k nearest neighbor model on the transformed feature vectors. The identification results using our proposed method showed that balanced and unbalanced walking condition could be recognized with high accuracy.

articleTitle: Modelling Mechanical Communication and Collective Motion of Cancer Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Understanding the communication mechanisms that drive collective behaviors in cancer is crucial for elucidating cancer progression and metastasis. To investigate communication mechanisms and their impacts on collective cell behaviors in can-cer, our previous study employed time-lapse imaging techniques on cancer cells placed on substrates containing fluorescent beads. In these experiments, we observed bead movements that reflect mechanical cell communication through substrate dynamics and collective cell motions. In this study, our objective is to develop a computational model to reproduce the experimental observations from our previous study. We demonstrated that the model developed in this paper substantiated previous experimental findings and established a foundation for further investigations into the communication mechanisms and collective behaviors in cancer.

articleTitle: Analysis of Spatio-Temporal Fishing Status of Large purse seine fishery Using AIS Data
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Globally., fishery resources are declining due to changes in the marine environment and overfishing. The methods used today have limitations in accurately identifying actual fishing areas. This study uses AIS trajectory data to identify the actual fishing areas of large purse seines and estimate spatio-temporal catch. AIS data from July 2019 to June 2022 were analyzed., and CPUE (Catch Per Unit Effort) was calculated using fish landing report data. Results indicated a southward shift in fishing grounds from 2019 to 2021, with increased CPUE in southwestern Jeju waters. This study highlights the effectiveness of AIS data in accurately estimating fishing patterns and catch, suggesting future research to incorporate environmental data for comprehensive analysis.

articleTitle: Automated Depth-Level Classification of Impacted Mandibular Third Molars Using Deep Learning on Panoramic X-Rays
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: The extraction of impacted mandibular third molars are common but complex procedure in oral surgery, often assessed using panoramic radiographs. This study proposes a deep learning-based approach for the automatic segmentation and depth-level classification of mandibular third molar teeth according to the Pell & Gregory classification method. Utilizing the YOLOv7 segmentation model, we segmented the molar teeth and mandible and developed an algorithm for depth-level classification. Despite the small training dataset of 315 images, our models achieved high performance, with Dice Similarity Coefficients (DSC) ranging from 0.9001 to 0.9120 for teeth segmentation and 0.9708 for mandible segmentation. The depth-level classification accuracy was 0.7794 for T32 teeth and 0.9118 for T17 teeth. The proposed method demonstrates the potential of deep learning in automating the assessment of third molar depth-level extraction difficulty, offering a scalable and accurate solution for clinical use.

articleTitle: Analysis of Sound Symbolism Appears In JoJo's Bizarre Adventure
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Sound symbolism is a phenomenon where specific sounds evoke specific images. However, not all aspects of sound symbolism have been clarified. This study investigates ono-matopoeia used as sound effects in comic books to propose a hypothesis on sound symbolism in this context. We focus on “JoJo's Bizarre Adventure Part 2 (JoJo),” known for its unique onomatopoeia. Our goal is to identify the acoustic characteristics of “JoJo-ness” and formulate a sound symbolism hypothesis specific to JoJo. Using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), we classified the onomatopoeia in JoJo and the Manga109 dataset to highlight the differences. Additionally, we conducted subjective experiments to further elucidate the acoustic characteristics of JoJo-ness.

articleTitle: Promoting Open Data Utilization in Infrastructure Management Through an Integrated System of Data Processing, Cloud Storage, and Visualization
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: During the rapid economic growth of Japan in the 1960s, the country's infrastructure development progressed swiftly. Since 2014, the Japanese government has mandated regular inspections of major urban infrastructure. This policy has resulted in the annual accumulation of substantial amounts of infrastructure inspection data. Two years prior to implementing this policy, the Japanese government also launched an open data initiative to encourage industry developers to utilize open data. However, this study observes that inconsistencies in data formatting and standards across different regions pose significant challenges to the utilization of this data. To address the obstacles hindering the use of open data, this study proposes an integrated system(Service Link Platform) for effectively managing and utilizing periodic transportation infrastructure inspection data which encompasses data collection, data format processing, cloud storage and transmission, and data utilization. This article will layout the manner in which the system employs a method for distributing data in JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) format to publicly manage bridge inspection data and ensure compatibility of data formats.

articleTitle: Accuracy Validation of Cardiac Disease Dataset with Cascaded ANFIS
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In this paper, we designed Cascaded ANFIS, which can be trained with a large number of input items and classes, and trained a Heartdisease dataset with 13 input items, which is difficult to train with regular ANFIS, and compared its performance with that of other AIs. The results showed that the accuracy of the presence/absence of heart disease by Cascaded ANFIS can achieve good generalization performance compared to the results of other AIs. In addition, the results of examining the change in accuracy of Cascaded ANFIS when the number of input items was reduced showed that when diagnosing the stage of heart disease, the dataset trained with 6 items selected in order of absolute value of correlation coefficient for the class variable to classify had higher accuracy, and the decision coefficient, which is the evaluation criterion for the diagnostic result of the level The coefficient of determination, which is a criterion for evaluating the diagnostic result of the level, was also shown to be higher.

Index Terms: Absolute Value Of The Correlation Coefficient

articleTitle: Prediction of Parametrial Invasion of Cervical Cancer Using Radiomics and CNN Features
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Parametrial invasion (PMI) is a key factor for the treatment planning of cervical cancers; however, PMI is difficult to accurately determine on preoperative images. In this study, we propose a PMI detection method using machine learning that aims to determine PMI from MR images independent of the physicians' diagnostic experience. The proposed method uses a mask image, created by delineating the tumor region, and dilated mask images. The PMI is determined using Radiomics features extracted from several types of MR images such as T1-weighted images (T1WI), T2-weighted images (T2WI), and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC). Then the Lasso regression extracts the important features. Experimental results using MR images of 13 PMI patients and 47 non-PMI patients showed that Logistic regression is best suited for PMI detection, using masked images and 9 pixels dilated masks. The comparison with the radiologist's diagnosis results showed that the proposed method outperformed all evaluation indices.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Development of an Underwater Environment Analysis System Based on Neural Network Using Omnidirectional Camera
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: The 30by30 goal was pledged at the G7 summit held in 2021. This goal aims to conserve more than 30 % of both terrestrial and marine areas as natural environment areas by 2030. In particular, observing and analyzing underwater environments is essential for preserving natural environment areas in marine areas. However, investigating underwater environments poses significant risks and requires substantial human resources. Consequently, there is a demand for systems that can measure and automatically analyze underwater conditions. This paper proposes the development of an underwater measurement system utilizing a waterproofed omnidirectional camera, along with a system for analyzing the collected data. Specifically, the system employs neural network-based techniques for fish detection and turbidity estimation.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Soldering Skill Using Fuzzy Inference
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This study addresses the challenge of manual soldering skill evaluation and transfer in the context of small and medium-sized enterprises where automation is less prevalent. Recognizing the limitations of current single-factor evaluation models, which primarily consider the soldering iron holding method, this research aims to develop a multifactor evaluation model incorporating additional aspects of the soldering process. The proposed model includes the general theory of time spent in soldering, focusing on the heating time of the base metal and the solder melting time as key factors. By integrating these statistical characteristics into a fuzzy inference model, alongside the traditional factor of soldering iron handling, a more comprehensive evaluation approach is achieved. This multifaceted model allows for a nuanced assessment of soldering skills and proposes improvement methods. Future work will involve verifying the model's accuracy with larger data sets and developing a system to facilitate skill evaluation and knowledge transfer, addressing the industry's labor shortage and the decline in skilled workers.

articleTitle: Effects of Gait Onomatopoeia on the Impression of Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In this study, we investigate whether the impression of a robot's gait can be altered by introducing onomatopoeic words such as phonomimes and phenomimes associated with its movement. Since mimetic words and sound words have high sound symbolism, the impression of gait onomatopoeia can potentially be formulated by using mimetic words and sound words instead of emotional words. We prepared two types of robot and four types of voice to investigate the impression of onomatopoeia and the effect of emotional expression through questionnaires, taking into consideration the impression changes by the difference of the robot's appearance and voice quality. Following cluster analysis of the questionnaire results, we classified the 14 types of onomatopoeia into four groups (busy onomatopoeia, powerful onomatopoeia, adorable onomatopoeia, and unenergetic onomatopoeia). Multiple comparisons of the means of the questionnaire results for each group showed that (1) busy onomatopoeia lowers the impression of happiness and sadness, (2) powerful onomatopoeia lowers happiness but raises width, (3) adorable onomatopoeia lowers anger, disgust, surprise, fear, and dynamism while raising softness, and (4) unenergetic onomatopoeia lowers anger, happiness, quickness, and dynamism while raising sadness.

articleTitle: Cancer Risk Evaluation with Diabetes Mellitus by a Large Medical Claims Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Although patients with diabetes mellitus are known to have an increased risk of developing cancer during follow-up, it is difficult to verify the risk due to diabetes mellitus of developing rare cancer at patients' life stage. Using a large dataset of medical claims, we examined the risk of developing cancer based on the presence or absence of diabetes mellitus in various cancer types, according to age and sex. The pattern of increased cancer risk due to diabetes mellitus differed in both men and women according to age and cancer locus. These results enable us to consider cancer screening strategies for diabetes mellitus patients adjusting age and gender.

articleTitle: Integer Programming Approaches to an Issue of Scheduling for a Truck-Drone Last-Mile Delivery System with Parcel Pickup Service
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In this paper, we consider a scheduling issue for parcel delivery and pickup services by a truck-drone last-mile delivery system. We are given a single carrier truck and multiple identical drones to serve a finite set of customers. The single carrier truck plays the role of a mobile depot for the drones, and it visits several stops in a given order of them. The given order of stops constitutes a fixed truck route, and the carrier truck is allowed to launch (resp., to retrieve) a drone to (resp., from) a customer at a stop. For each sortie of a drone, the launching stop and the retrieving stop must be the same. The load capacity of a drone is limited to one, and for a sortie of a drone at a stop, there are three options: (i) only deliver a parcel to a customer, (ii) only pick up a parcel from a customer, and (iii) deliver a parcel to a customer, and then pick up a parcel from a customer. The scheduling problem asks to find an assignment of customers to drones with sortie options and a choice of a truck stop for each sortie in the assignment. The objective is to minimize the total duration of the carrier truck over all the stops, which is equivalent to minimizing the makespan. In this paper, we first propose an extended integer program for the case with both delivery and pickup services from an existing one for the case with delivery service only. We also conduct numerical experiments to demonstrate the solution quality of the proposed integer program by utilizing an integer programming solver, and report the results.

articleTitle: Generalization of Rough-Set-Based Attribute Reduction by Using Purity Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Attribute reduction is a data analysis method based on rough set theory. It is defined by preserving various measures and/or structures derived from rough set models. In this study, we propose attribute reduction based on purity functions in the probabilistic rough set model. The purity function evaluates the uncertainty associated with objects, whether they belong to a target set. We study the relationship between conventional methods of attribute reduction and purity-based methods.

articleTitle: EC-Net: Efficient Compound Network with Dendritic Learning for Cataract Eye Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: As the leading cause of visual impairment and blindness, automatic methods for diagnosing cataracts from retinal images are desired. With the advancement of computer technology, deep learning-based approaches have demonstrated superior performance compared to traditional manual methods. These algorithms are particularly advantageous in terms of conserving human and material resources and minimizing the dependency on clinical expertise. However, existing methods often struggle with extracting the non-linear characteristics inherent in cataract data. To alleviate this challenge, we propose a novel Efficient-dendritic Cataract-detection Network (EC-Net), which integrates the Dendritic Neuron Model for efficient and accurate detection of cataracts. This network leverages the nonlinear properties of dendritic neurons in conjunction with advanced deep learning feature extraction techniques to enhance the accuracy of cataract identification. Experimental results on publicly available datasets demonstrate that EC-Net significantly outperforms traditional models in the classification of cataract fundus images, providing a promising solution for medical image classification and supporting auxiliary diagnosis.

articleTitle: CAWA: Correlation-Based Adaptive Weight Adjustment via Effective Fields for Debiasing
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In real-world image classification tasks, neural networks often encounter significant challenges due to unexpected or deceptive correlations and biases inherent in the dataset. These biases can emerge from disproportionate data distributions, causing models to generalize poorly to new, unseen data. Such data distribution issues are particularly problematic compared to more balanced datasets because they lead the model to rely on bias attributes rather than intrinsic attributes. Ideally, the model should classify based on intrinsic attributes, but due to the influence of bias attributes, frequent misclassification occurs. Such biases compromise the fairness and accuracy of the model, especially in critical scenarios such as medical diagnosis, autonomous driving, or criminal justice, where misclassification can have significant consequences. To address these challenges, we propose an innovative two-stage approach aimed at mitigating bias more effectively and efficiently.

articleTitle: A Study of Nursing Behavior Using Agent Expressing a Sense of Mission and Empathy: with Virtual Appearance with Robot Hand
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a nurse agent system that can provide emotional support to users to solve the future shortage of nurses and the lack of systems that provide emotional support to patients. For emotional support for patients, we implemented an agent system linked to a robot hand that can express empathy for the user and a sense of mission to help the patient during the cuddling behavior. The results showed that the agent's cuddling behavior, with expressions of empathy and a sense of mission, increased the degree of the patient's relaxation and made the patient feel less pain. Furthermore, we confirmed the possibility that the acceptance and humanity of the agent's expressions could be enhanced by using both expressions of empathy and a sense of mission.

articleTitle: The Impact of Tournament Size on the Performance of Evolutionary Multi-Objective and Many-Objective Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Tournament selection is an operator used in many evolutionary multi-objective (EMO) algorithms. The tournament size is a parameter of tournament selection, and it is generally considered that increasing the tournament size improves conver-gence while reducing diversity. To the best of our knowledge, there is no literature that analyzes the relationship between EMO algorithms and tournament size, and it is not clear what impact increasing the tournament size has on EMO algorithms. In many past studies, the tournament size has been fixed at 2 without a clear rationale. However, the likelihood that 2 is the optimal tournament size is low. Therefore, this paper investigates the performance of EMO algorithms using tournament selection when the tournament size is changed for various benchmark problems. Through experiments, we demonstrate that increasing the tournament size beyond 2 yields better results for many benchmark problems. Additionally, we experimentally show that AGEMOEAIYITS, which combines AGEMOEAII and Increase Tournament Selection, where the tournament size dynamically increases with each generation, performs well on many bench-mark problems.

articleTitle: Self-Organizing Method for Word Embedding
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In natural language processing, word embedding is essential for vectorizing word features. Mikolov et al. proposed Word2vec, which uses neural networks to learn relationships between words from large text corpora. Word2vec is known for its fast and efficient learning, but there is a risk of overfitting when embedding with small datasets. In this research, we propose a word embedding method based on self-organizing techniques. By leveraging the properties of self-organization, we aim to develop an effective method for constructing local knowledge in small datasets. The primary advantages of our method include its ability to handle small datasets more effectively than traditional word embedding models like Word2Vec. Its capability of preserving the topological relationships between words, and its enhanced performance in both accuracy and stability, as demonstrated in our experiments. This method also provides better visualization and interpretability of the word embeddings.

articleTitle: Improving Prototype Intelligent Tactical Board for Rugby Sevens
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In the last decade, advanced tactical understanding has become increasingly necessary for players and coaches in rugby, as has been the case in other team sports. Against this background, we have prototyped an intelligent tactical board tool for rugby sevens. This tool can compute a single normative offensive sequence derived from players’ position and velocity information, consisting of running plays and hand-passing plays. The computed sequence serves as a reference for enhancing the tactical understanding of players and coaches. However, considering practical usage situations, displaying multiple offensive sequences is expected to be more suitable, as it provides a broader range of options. Yet, this is difficult to achieve due to the limitations of the simple branch and bound algorithm currently applied. Therefore, in this study, we enhance this prototype tool so that it can compute multiple normative offensive sequences. Moreover, to make the computed sequences more intuitively understandable, this study newly incorporates an integration function with a commercially available 3D visualization tool for rugby plays to this prototype tool. To confirm the functionality of the improved tool, we conduct a validation test using a real formation example from a video of an actual rugby sevens match.

articleTitle: Probabilistic Model Building Evolutionary Algorithm Using the Same Type and Size of Model for Any Binary Optimization Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: We propose <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$a$</tex> new probabilistic model building evolutionary algorithm that uses the same type and size of probabilistic model for any binary optimization problems. The proposed method represents a population as a binary matrix for any binary optimization problems and solves a given problem by transforming the population in the form of matrix to better one with 512 production rules of cellular automaton. Concretely, the proposed method builds a probabilistic model for generating new solution candidates while applying the 512 production rules to the matrix representing the population. The probabilistic model consists of the 512 inverse production rules and their application probabilities. The strong point of the proposed method is to be able to transform any binary optimization problems to the same size of 512-bit production rule optimization problem. Since the proposed method treats any binary optimization problems in a unified manner, we can easily explore a robust method for various binary optimization problems as the proposed method with particular configurations. As the first evaluation of the proposed method, we apply the proposed method to the same kind but different sizes of problems. The results show that depending strongly on the bit patterns of the global optima, the proposed method with the same configurations realizes a good scalability of the number of function evaluations required for obtaining near optimum to the problem size growth.

articleTitle: Graph Convolutional Networks Approach for Alzheimer's Disease Stage Classification Using Multimodal Data
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: With the advancement of medical technology, the global population is aging and this is expected to increase the number of dementia patients. Alzheimer's disease (AD) is the most common cause of dementia and is a heterogeneous, neurodegenerative brain disorder. Due to the lack of a complete cure, early diagnosis is crucial to slow the progression of symptoms. Mild cognitive impairment (MCI), an intermediate state between normal cognition (NC) and dementia, also necessitates early diagnosis because it can progress to AD. In reality, doctors diagnose AD stage by considering multiple types of data such as brain imaging, demographic information, genetic tests, and neuropsychological tests. Therefore, AD stage classification models need to learn these multimodal data. In this study, we proposed applying the graph convolutional network (GCN) to population graphs constructed by using cosine similarity, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L1$</tex>-norm, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-norm on multimodal data for AD stage classification. The multimodal data consisted of F -18 florbetaben (FBB) amyloid brain positron emission tomography (PET) images, demographic information, and genetic test, and neuropsychological test data. Different dimensional FBB PET images and non-image data were matched by using a multimodal fusion method utilizing a 3D dense convolutional network. The proposed methods are investigated through cross-validation with support vector machine, random forest, and multilayer percep- tron models. The results suggest that the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> 1 -norm leads to better performance of GCN in AD stage classification due to its better robustness against outliers and its ability to account for the heterogeneity of AD compared to cosine similarity and L2 -norm.

articleTitle: Genetic Algorithm with Efficient Selection Using Pareto Front Modeling and Data Envelopment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: There exist various multi-objective optimization problems(MOPs) in the real world that require acquiring diverse solutions efficiently. Various multi-objective evolutionary algorithms (MOEAs) have been proposed to solve MOPs. Generally, in MOEAs, the same score criterion is conducted in Survival and Tournament Selection. In Survival, parent selection score should be conducted to ensure convergence and diversity, and in Tournament Selection, the selection score of individuals for crossover should be conducted to select individuals with high convergence compared to other individuals. Therefore, evolutionary computation algorithms are expected to perform efficient exploration while maintaining diversity. In this work, we propose an efficient selection algorithm using data envelopment analysis and pareto front modeling. In Survival, we perform an evaluation using existing methods to ensure high convergence and diversity, and in Tournament Selection, we use the data envelopment analysis method to select individuals with high convergence compared to other individuals. This allows us to balance both high convergence and diversity. Moreover, by implementing Pareto front modeling, we were also successful in addressing the issue of assuming convexity in the data envelopment analysis method. In comparison using the HV METRIC on the WFG and DTLZ benchmark functions, the proposed method showed superior results compared to the existing methods of NSGA-II, AGE-MOEA-II, and DEA-GA with the exception of 9-objective functions.

articleTitle: Debiasing CLIP with Feature Augmentation and Selective Update to Preserve Zero-Shot Capability
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Vision-language models, including CLIP, have shown impressive performance across various tasks. However, these models often struggle to distinguish meaningful features from spurious correlations in dataset biases, resulting in gen-eralization issues. Mitigating these biases without compromising CLIP's core strengths for zero-shot performance is crucial but has been overlooked. We propose a novel adversarial training method to debias CLIP, combining PGD on the projection layer for feature augmentation and Selective Update for Debiasing (SUD). Our method targets the projection layer, using minimally distorted feature augmentation and selective update strategy guided by model predictions. PGD uses the embedding layer's gradients to generate biased features that induce misclassifications with minimal distortion. SUD applies different objective functions to refine features based on prediction accuracy. These methods effectively mitigate bias by training on misclassified samples and preserve the existing embedding space. Experiments confirm our method improves model robustness against biases while maintaining zero-shot performance. This approach offers a promising solution for debiasing vision-language models without degradation in performance.

articleTitle: Real-time Support for Solution Search in Human-based Evolutionary Computation
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: We propose a method to extract important words common to good solution candidates in human-based evolutionary computation, like building blocks in genetic algorithms, and present them to the participants in a realtime manner. We also propose a method to obtain and present words similar to the important ones. Furthermore, we propose a method to measure the similarity between participants using the important words for each participant and present it to the participants. All of the proposed methods help participants solve problems by reducing the cognitive load of finding key words and persons. We implement those methods into a human-based evolutionary computation system and evaluate the proposed methods through human subject experiments using the system. The experimental results show that although the evaluation result to the outputs from the system incorporating the methods by a third party is not so good, the system is shown to be useful for participants to create solutions.

articleTitle: Greeting Gesture Analysis Using Boosting Algorithms and SHAP
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Recently, studies related to human activity recognition have developed which have been applied in various fields. In that field Machine learning and deep learning techniques have been widely used for several classification and prediction tasks. However, the first problem is that there is rarely any research on human activities that reflect the culture of a region, such as greeting gestures. Second, there are few studies that do not provide models resulting from the classification or prediction process using machine learning, which can result in a lack of understanding of how a model from machine learning is generated. This study aims to predict Japanese greeting gestures (eshaku, keirei, saikeirei, waving hand) and Indonesian (placing both hands in front of the chest) using Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Gradient Boosting. Then, represent the model of the learning machine using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to find out how the learning machine obtain a model. Our findings show the efficacy of this method and show that the model not only predicts greeting gestures with high accuracy but also offers a transparent understanding of the factors influencing its predictions, thus enhancing the interpretability and applicability of machine learning in recognizing culturally significant human activities. In the future, we plan to use machine learning and other Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) methods to study human activities with cultural concepts such as greeting gestures in different styles, create more greeting gesture-based human activity datasets, and examine the ethical implications or considerations of using machine learning in cultural contexts to respect cultural differences.

articleTitle: A Study on Predicting Ratings System through Sentiment Analysis and Clustering of Coupang Product Reviews
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: With the expansion of e-commerce platforms, online reviews have become increasingly important. Users often decide on purchases based on reviews and ratings. This study notes that reviews with identical ratings can differ in emotional content and hypothesizes that overall satisfaction can be inferred from these emotions.
