The aim is to develop a system to quantify satisfaction based on review content, especially when ratings are absent. This approach addresses situations where reviews lack ratings or users struggle to rate products despite providing feedback. We crawled product reviews from Coupang and performed sentiment analysis using a BERT model tailored for Korean. The sentiment analysis results were clustered using six different algorithms, and the outcomes were evaluated. The study explored the best methodology among 30 combinations of clustering algorithms and hyper-parameters. For evaluation, ‘accuracy’ and ‘mean absolute error’ were used as external metrics to compare with actual ratings, while the ‘silhouette coefficient’ was used as an internal metric to assess cluster clarity. Agglomerative Clustering showed the highest performance in external metrics but lower internal metric performance. Spectral Clustering demonstrated well-balanced and excellent performance across all metrics.

articleTitle: Simplified Multiplayer Battle Game-inspired Optimizer with Diverse Search Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: We propose two modifications to the standard multiplayer battle game-inspired optimizer (MBGO) to simplify its search framework and enhance its performance. Specifically, the first modification changes the original serial two-stage search to a parallel approach, where individuals probabilistically choose to execute one of the stages instead of both. The second modification introduces additional new search strategies for generating diversified offspring individuals in the two stages, while retaining the original search strategies. To evaluate the performance of our proposal, we compared the MBGO combined with two proposed modifications against several classic algorithms using the function collections of CEC2017 and CEC2020. The experimental results demonstrate that the improved MBGO is highly competitive, particularly with increasing dimensionality, where the performance improvement becomes more pronounced.

articleTitle: Video Generation with Single Flame Image and Wind Direction Information
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In recent years, the shortage of human resources in the animation and video production industry has become a sig-nificant issue, leading to a demand for efficient video generation methods. Deep learning-based video generation techniques are seen as a potential solution, with research focusing on generating natural phenomena videos from single images. Progress has been made in developing video generation networks that incorporate external forces, such as wind, into the models. However, there is still a need for further advancements in creating networks that can more accurately and effectively respond to the creator's intent and handle complex natural phenomena. In this paper, we constructed a video generation network that uses a single image of a flame and wind direction information as input to generate natural flame videos considering the external force of wind. This network was trained through a two-stage process based on VQ-VAE (Vector Quantized-Variational AutoEncoder) and Transformer models. The network demonstrated the ability to capture the relationship between flame motion and wind. The videos generated by this network accurately depicted changes in flame behavior due to wind direction, showcasing the high accuracy of the video generation. Furthermore, the Frechet Video Distance (FVD) index achieved by our network was comparable to those reported in similar studies, indicating competitive performance.

articleTitle: Color and Sentiment: A Study of Emotion-Based Color Palettes in Marketing
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: It's widely recognized that the colors used in branding significantly impact how a brand is perceived. This research explores the influence of color in logos on consumer perception and emotional response. We investigate the associations between color usage and emotional responses in food and beverage marketing. Using a dataset of 644 companies, we analyzed the dominant colors in brand logos using k-means clustering to develop distinct color palettes. Concurrently, we extracted customer sentiments and emotions from Google Maps reviews of these companies (n=30,069), categorizing them into five primary emotions: Happiness, Anger, Sadness, Fear, and Surprise. These emotional responses were further categorized into four intensity levels: Low, Medium, Strong, and Very Strong, using a fuzzy sets approach. Our methodology involved correlating specific color palettes with the predominant emotional reactions associated with each brand. By merging the color palettes of companies that elicited similar emotional responses, we identified unique color palettes corresponding to each emotional category. Our findings suggest that among the food companies analyzed, the dominant emotion was Happiness, with no instances of Anger. The colors red and gray were prevalent across all emotional categories, indicating their importance in branding. Specific color-emotion correlations confirmed by our research include associations of yellow with Happiness, blue with Sadness, and bright colors with Surprise. This study highlights the critical role of color in shaping consumer attitudes. The study findings have practical implications for brand designers in the food industry.

articleTitle: BMA for the BMA: Boosting Mobility Analysis for the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration via Automated Pedestrian Counting from CCTV
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: The objective of detecting and counting people using the CCTV camera on the footpath is to facilitate and reduce the time required to count the number of people traveling in pedestrian areas without having to actually visit the area. This paper uses the head detection technique to solve the problem of overlapping objects, YOLOv8n for detection and BoT-SORT for object tracking. A program was developed to assist the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration in counting the number of people within the region of interest and visualizing the statistics. Users can view statistics in the form of visual charts to compare the maximum number of people in each period by importing the video into the program. Users can also view historical statistics from previously imported videos. This program enables users to monitor pedestrian traffic in each area, providing valuable insights for urban planning decisions.

articleTitle: Enhancing Formation Analysis Using Multi-layer Graph Convolutional Neural Networks and Geometric Formation Features
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: We have previously proposed a formation analysis method using multi-layer graph convolutional neural networks with geometric formation features as input. In addition, this analysis method has been validated by applying it to a classification problem of soccer shooting scenes, and the results have been demonstrated its validity. However, when considering the context of team sports, it was considered that there is room for enhancement in the graph convolutional layers used in the method. Therefore, in this study, we propose new graph convolutional layers that are considered more effective for team sports. Furthermore, we validate the analysis method incorporating the proposed layers by applying it to a soccer shooting scene classification problem. We also conduct an ablation study on the adj acency information input.

articleTitle: UNet-Based Land Cover Segmentation With Ensembled Encoder for Fine Details Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Satellite technology has made it possible to capture Earth's surface with very high accuracy in the centimeter range. This is crucial for remote sensing tasks, particularly land use mapping, which is frequently used for urban planning and tracking land-use changes. However, processing remote sensing data is quite challenging, where several objects have similarities in color, shape, or texture, which can impact how the model separates objects into corresponding labels. In addition, due to extensive spatial remote sensing coverage, class imbalance becomes a significant issue, which impacts model decisions when classifying the objects. To overcome this issue, we proposed a modified U-Net model using pre-trained as the backbone for the encoder to reduce overfitting and help the model extract better information from pre-trained weights. In addition, the model will be trained using the joint loss consisting of dice loss adapted for multiclass problems to balance recall and precision in classification and focal loss, an improved cross-entropy specifically for class imbalance tasks. Then, we select three models as weak learners in an ensemble architecture that uses a majority voting strategy. Our experiments show the best results with Dice and mIoU of 86.71% and 77.25%, respectively, for the GID-5 dataset and 76.14% and 63.68% for the WHDLD dataset.

articleTitle: Verbal Description Focusing on Physical Properties of Real-World Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In recent years, prediction models for the real world have been widely proposed. Most research that deals with the recognition and prediction of the real world generates prediction results from visual predictions such as changes in pixels or numerical changes in physical simulators, and there are few models that can predict based on both visual and physical characteristics, as humans can. Therefore, in this study, we constructed a new prediction model based on both visual information and physical characteristics in the environment by integrating the mechanism of Variational Temporal Abstraction (VTA), which extracts change points in the observation environment from visual information, into PreCNet. Furthermore, in order to make the prediction results interpretable, we generated the inferred prediction content as a sentence. In addition, we verified whether the generated sentences could explain collision situations in as much detail as a human being when given physical common sense about the environment, such as the movement and mass of objects.

articleTitle: Multi-Scale Local Feature Fusion-Based Polyp Segmentation Method in Colonoscopy Images
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Polyps are unusual growths in colon or rectum and can develop into colorectal cancer (CRC). The precise segmentation of polyps in medical images is crucial for early diagnosis and effective treatment planning. Traditional approaches rely heavily on manual delineation by radiologists, a method that is time-consuming and prone to variability. Consequently, there is growing interest in leveraging deep learning technologies to automate and improve segmentation process. In this paper, we introduce Strategic Tri-Attention ResNet (StarNet), an innovative approach designed to enhance polyp segmentation through a multi-scale attention mechanism. Our comprehensive experimental evaluations reveal that StarNet surpasses many classic methods with good performance in polyp segmentation tasks, especially in capturing detailed boundary features. By integrating multi-scale attention mechanisms, StarNet provides a promising solution for precise and efficient polyp segmentation, ultimately contributing to better clinical outcomes in CRC diagnosis and treatment.

articleTitle: Energy-Based Continuous Time Series Probability Model with Latent Stochastic Process
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Astract- This paper presents a new energy-based continuous time series probability model that has stochastic process in its latent dynamics. Because the model assuming its output is used for connecting a vector space such as embedding space and latent dynamics, one of the possible application of the present study is to predict sequence of segments such as in the human motion behavior recognition. The present model gives joint distribution of all variable, therefore, it has the property to generate learned sequence without conditioning any values including initial state. This property overcomes existing problem in initial value condition for frequently applied time series model such as recurrent neural network. Furthermore, energy-based continuous formulation gives us consistent method for both learning and estimating the state by the gradient descent and its derivative methods. Such consistent method is not proposed in existing study. In this paper, the model formulation, gradient estimator, and its learning method is shown. Experiments on synthetic data is given, and the validity of the proposed model and method discussed.

articleTitle: A Shape-Based Similarity Calculation Method for Cost Estimation of Large Forged Steel Products
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This study aims to estimate the cost of large forged steel products by calculating similarity through both shape and numerical factors, such as weight, maximum horizontal length, and maximum diameter. The estimation process intends to simulate expert judgment about manufacturing and fabrication cost similarity, rather than relying solely on geometric and numerical data. We propose an original approach that integrates shape similarity via deep metric learning methods with numerical similarity. To validate our method, the simulation results were compared with the judgments of an experienced professional at an actual steelmaking site. The results of the analysis identified the improvement of reproducibility by emphasizing the complexity of the body shape as a future issue. Specifically, focusing on body shape improved reproducibility within the top three similar products by 36% compared to considering overall shape, and further emphasizing complexity decreased reproducibility by 20%.

articleTitle: Extraction and Classification of Lung Nodule Features Using Fusion Method of Self-Supervised Encoder Learning and Supervised Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Classifying lung nodules as benign or malignant using CT images is crucial for the diagnosis of early-stage lung cancer and can significantly enhance survival rates. This paper proposes a method for extracting and classifying features of lung nodules through self-supervised encoder learning and supervised transfer learning to improve the distinguishing characteristics of lung nodules. Initially, the extracted nodule patches are perturbed to generate two corresponding augmented patches, which are utilized to learn global features using a contrastive learning network. Subsequently, one of the augmented patches is divided into non-overlapping segments and masked with a random mask. Reconstruction learning captures fine-grained local features through the reconstruction task. Furthermore, adversarial training directs the reconstruction learning process to yield more realistic information. Finally, the parameters of the pre-trained encoder are employed in a supervised classification task to categorize nodules as malignant or benign. Validation of the proposed method on the public LIDC-IDRI dataset demonstrates an accuracy of 89.0%, representing a 5.5% improvement over the state-of-the-art method.

articleTitle: Combining TL and KD for Object Detection Model Compression
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In modern society, object detection tasks have become extremely important due to their numerous applications in fields such as autonomous driving, surveillance, and healthcare. Real-time detection is particularly crucial for many applications. However, with the advancements in deep learning-based object detection methods, high performance often comes with high computational resource requirements, posing challenges for real-time monitoring, especially on resource-constrained devices. To address this issue, we study model compression using both transfer learning (TL) and knowledge distillation (KD). Specifically, we use the YOLOv5n model as a test case to show the basic idea for improving the performance of a small student model using a larger dataset for TL and a larger model for KD. As for KD, we further investigate feature-based and output-based KD. Experimental results show that the small student model can be improved significantly using TL and KD, with the mean Average Precision (mAP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.</inf><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>) being increased by 13.28% compared to the baseline model. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of TL and KD in achieving high detection performance while reducing computational demands, making them suitable for various real-world applications.

articleTitle: Health Classification on Oil Palm UAV Images Using Machine Learning with Features Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: The sheer size of oil palm plantations is causing challenges in managing the plantation efficiently and effectively. Among the many challenges affecting the palms, timely disease control is crucial in maintaining high yield and sustainable agriculture practice. This paper investigates the health monitoring of oil palms using images taken with unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), enabling proactive intervention and targeted disease management. Based on 2002 real-world oil palm images provided by the industry, support vector machine (SVM) optimized with a radial basis function (RBF) kernel was able to achieve an Fl score of 0.975 on test data and a macro Fl score of 0.88 on inference data, paving the way for its application in large scale diseased tree identification in the plantation.

articleTitle: A Bias in Training Data Degrades the Quality of Variable Importance Scores of Random Forests
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: The random forest, a machine learning technique, offers several preferable features that have drawn the interest and focus of researchers. In practically applying the random forest, we found that the training data containing many examples similar to each other degraded the quality of the importance scores. To overcome this harmful effect, we have proposed a method that assigns weight values to the training data. Our experimental results showed that the quality decline of the importance scores could be resolved by considering the weight values determined by the weighting method in the training of the random forest. It turned out, however, that this harmful effect and the effectiveness of the weighting method in overcoming it could only be confirmed on a specified task. Although the main purpose of machine learning techniques is to obtain a good approximation of the target function, the importance scores are often used to extract information from the given data. From what we can see, the degradation in the quality of the importance scores is not yet widely known. In this study we attempted to reveal the conditions under which this harmful effect occurs. We confirmed that the weighting approach works well even in other problems.

articleTitle: Video Popularity in Social Media: Impact of Emotions, Raw Features and Viewer Comments
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: The Internet has significantly affected the increase of social media users. Nowadays, informative content is presented along with entertainment on the web. Highlighting environmental issues on social networks is crucial, given their significance as major global problems. This study examines the popularity determinants for short environmental videos on social media, focusing on the comparative influence of raw video features and viewer engagement metrics. We collected a dataset of videos along with associated popularity metrics such as likes, views, shares, and comments per day. We also extracted video characteristics, including duration, text post length, emotional and sentiment analysis using the VADER and text2emotion models, and color palette brightness. Our analysis consisted of two main experiments: one evaluating the correlation between raw video features and popularity metrics and another assessing the impact of viewer comments and their sentiments and emotions on video popularity. We employed a ridge regression classifier with standard scaling to predict the popularity, categorizing videos as popular or not based on the median views and likes per day. The findings reveal that viewer comments and reactions (accuracy of 0.8) have a more substantial influence on video popularity compared to raw video features (accuracy of 0.67). Significant correlations include a positive relationship between the emotion of sadness in posts and the number of likes and negative correlations between sentiment scores, and both likes and shares. This research highlights the complex relationship between content features and public perception in shaping the popularity of environmental messages on social media.

articleTitle: Driver's Perception of Autonomous Cornering Control Based on a Sense of Circular Vision Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Recently, Research and Development of autonomous driving technology are rapidly conducted in the automobile industry. Expectations for automated driving technology are growing. However, some people have concerns about comfort and safety of driving systems. One reason is that the difference between perception of automated driving and the perception of human driving. Current automated driving technology is considered human perception. However, current automated cornering control doesn't consider human perception. Previous studies have defined and modeled Sense of Circular Vision (SoCV) as the sensation perceived during cornering behavior. Moreover, automatic turning control has been developed using model predictive control based on a SoCV model. In this paper, we evaluate how people feel by the autonomous cornering control based on the SoCV model using a VR simulator.

articleTitle: How Close has Computer Vision Become to Human Image Cognition?
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: It has been shown that Computer Vision Models (CVMs), which perform supervised learning (SL) using a large amount of labeled image data such as ImageNet, are quite like the human sense of visual similarity (VS). Since labeling is expensive, learning methods that do not require labeled data have been desired. Following CLIP, which uses contrastive learning between images and text, self-supervised learning (SSL) models such as BEiT have recently been released one after another. We analyzed how close CVMs approximate human sense. We investigated three types of photo sets, 100 garden landscapes, 242 townscapes, and 200 student life photos. Photos were quantified by many participants manually measuring the inter-photo VS. We selected the synthesized CVM that correlates best with VS from 25 types of pre-trained CVMs by softmax regression. We found that the best CVM for each photo set varied significantly. SL semantic segmentation and SSL EVA02 were effective for garden landscapes. SSL DINO and EV A02 were effective for townscapes. SL ImageNet-21K-P, CoAtNet, MLP Mixer, SSL BEiT, and CLIP-LAION-400M were effective for student life photos. It was surprising that CLIP-LAION-2B and SEER, which were pre-trained on a huge number of images, were ineffective on any photo set.

articleTitle: Diffusion-Based Augmentation for Lung Cancer Risk Prediction from Temporal CT Images
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Cancer risk prediction based on CT images of a patient taken at multiple time points in the past has become an emerging research topic. While deep learning methods yield promising results, they require a large amount of temporally sequenced data for reliable performance. Acquiring such time-series data is expensive and time-consuming. Hence, data aug-mentation based on a small, annotated, and temporally sequenced medical image dataset is essential to cancer risk prediction. This paper introduces a novel diffusion-based method for augmenting temporal medical images with an application to lung cancer risk prediction. Specifically, we develop our approach based on a conditional diffusion model owing to its high flexibility of condition design. We generate target images of a patient for training by overlaying tumors recently detected and masked by eroded segmentation maps onto CT images taken earlier to simulate tumor growth. Specifically, our conditional diffusion model is trained by using CT images taken in the first or second year, along with tumor segmentation maps in the third year, as well as the generated target images. Three distinct generation strategies are designed by using different combinations of CT images and eroded segmentation maps as conditions to synthesize lung CT images, hence diversifying and enriching the training set. Experimental results demonstrate that learning using 25 % of training data together with our augmented data achieves comparable performance to that using 100% of training data.

articleTitle: Predicting Models of Per Day Inbound/Outbound Baggage at Terminal 2 of Taoyuan International Airport During 2019–2023
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This study aims to develop a data-driven predictive model for daily inbound and outbound baggage volumes at Terminal 2 of Taoyuan International Airport. The research spans 2019 to 2023, encompassing data from the COVID-19 pandemic period. The study considers multiple influencing factors by establishing regression models, including daily passenger numbers, COVID-19 impact, seasonal variations, and policy factors. The models demonstrate high accuracy with R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> values exceeding 0.98. Key findings reveal that the average daily outbound baggage (5,388 pieces) significantly exceeds inbound (3,239 pieces), with outbound passenger numbers having a more significant influence on baggage volume (coefficient 1.045) compared to inbound (coefficient 0.918). Sensitivity analysis shows that changes in passenger numbers have the most significant impact on baggage volume, followed by COVID-19, the 2022 effect, and the January effect. Notably, COVID-19 impacted outbound baggage (-4,680 pieces) more than inbound (-2,517 pieces). The study also established high and low thresholds for baggage handling, with 90% and 68% thresholds for outbound baggage at 36,844 and 25,573 pieces, respectively, and 31,123 and 20,812 pieces for inbound. The model developed in this study accurately predicts daily baggage volumes and serves for long-term planning, such as forecasting inbound baggage for January 2024. These findings give airport managers valuable decision-support tools to optimize resource allocation, improve service quality, and prepare for potential disruptions, enhancing operational efficiency and passenger satisfaction.

articleTitle: Protein Secondary Structure Prediction using N-Grams and 1-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In this study, we initiated an approach to predict Protein Secondary Structure Prediction (PSSP) by using n-grams modeling, namely <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n$</tex> adjacent amino acid sequences, to represent the amino acid sequence and 1-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). We compare n-grams with a one-hot encoding approach and find that n-grams provide better performance. The analysis results show that bigrams are more effective than trigrams in describing protein amino acid sequence patterns. We also combine it with the PSSM profile feature to improve model performance. The results of this study reveal that the n-grams approach, especially bigrams, in combination with PSSM, can produce more accurate protein secondary structure predictions than previous models, with superior accuracy evaluations of Q8 68.1 % and Q3 82.75<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> on the CB513 dataset.

articleTitle: Effectiveness of RSNPs in Networks Construction of Educational Support Robots
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In recent years, robots that interact with humans, such as guide robots, have been increasingly used in commercial and public facilities. In order to promote the development of the robot industry, a robot communication protocol RSNP (Robot Service Network Protocol) has been developed based on the existing HTTP network protocol. RSNP can unify communications between robots and servers while taking advantage of the Web service feature of HTTP. However, the practicality and effectiveness of robots using RSNP have not been fully verified. In this paper, we examine the effectiveness of network communication using RSNP in an educational support robot. The amount of data that needs to be communicated during a single learning session, such as the learner's facial expressions and grades, is large for an educational support robot, and secure and stable communication is required. In this experiments, we compared the communication processing of the aforementioned data between RSNP and HTTP. The experimental results show that RSNP is capable of secure communication at a processing speed equivalent to that of HTTP, excluding the connection processing time. Therefore, it is suggested that RSNP is more effective than HTTP for communication with educational robots.

articleTitle: Multiobjective Branch-and-Cut Method with Shared Cutting Plane Information: A Case Study on Optimizing Garbage Collection
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This paper presents an application of the Multi-Objective Branch-and-Bound based on Decomposition (MOBB/D) method for Branch-and-Cut, combining branch-and-bound and cutting-plane methods. Traditionally, multi-objective branch-and-bound methods for multi-objective mixed-integer linear programming problems struggle with the large number of Pareto-optimal solutions. MOBB/D addresses this by decomposing multi-objective problems into single-objective subproblems using weight vectors and applying branch-and-bound to each, with information sharing between nearby subproblems. In this paper, we customize the MOBB/D method for Branch-and-Cut to achieve an efficient search by sharing cutting plane information in MOBB/D. We demonstrate our approach with a case study on garbage collection planning in Muroran City, Hokkaido, Japan. This case study combines facility location and route optimization within a multi-objective framework, balancing the burdens on residents and garbage collection workers. Numerical experiments compare execution times and solutions with and without cutting plane sharing, and visualize the impact of different objective balance preferences on route optimization. The results show substantial efficiency gains and provide practical insights for multi-objective optimization in urban planning.

articleTitle: Improving Sign Gesture Recognition Using Bi-LSTM Attention Model with Optimal Point Cloud Frame Range
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: For individuals who are hard of hearing and not proficient in sign language, assistance is vital for understanding and communication. This research aims to support them using machine learning models to recognize sign language gestures and translate them into texts. This study employs a millimeter wave (mmWave) radar sensor due to its non-invasive nature, privacy protection, and insensitive to illumination and weather to capture frames of a sequence of sign gestures performed. Those frames captured at specific time steps contain point cloud data. Subsequently, the frame range representing the temporal information of each gesture performed, initially varying between [11–120], was optimized to [30–54], improving LSTM model accuracy from 88.3% to 89.2% while reducing gesture samples from 800 to 700 roughly. Two additional models, Bi-LSTM and Bi-LSTM with Attention, were constructed to improve accuracy. Their accuracies improved from 88.7% and 89.86% to 91.7% and 92.3% after frame range optimization.

articleTitle: Universal vs. Contextual Color-Emotion Associations: A Fuzzy Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Color is the most influential visual factor that evokes emotional responses in humans. Nowadays, we can obtain color-emotion associations using various methods, including machine learning, deep learning, and fuzzy sets. This paper aims to identify to what extent these associations can be universal. We extend our previous work on color-emotion associations in art by examining these relationships in three additional datasets, each labeled with specific emotions. Utilizing fuzzy sets and logic approach, we extracted color-emotion associations from these new datasets and compared them using Jaccard and cosine similarity metrics to determine their resemblance to associations found in traditional art. Additionally, we conducted an experiment with AI-generated art images to compare color-emotion associations produced by artists versus artificial intelligence. Our results suggest that while most emotions exhibit universal color associations, emotions such as sadness, fear, shame, and trust display varying associations depending on the context. This variability could be attributed to these emotions being influenced less by color and more by the objects depicted within the art. Our findings highlight the complex interplay between color and emotional perception and suggest that while some color-emotion associations are universal, others are context-dependent. This study deepens our understanding of the emotional dimensions of color and broadens the applicability of these insights in fields like design and artificial intelligence.

articleTitle: Enhancing Feature Prediction in Image Generation Models via Task Arithmetic
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In the task of generating images, various image generation models have been developed. “Stable Diffusion” has garnered significant attention for its ability to generate high-quality derivative images with minimal artifacts. However, developing various derivative models requires extensive trial and error and considerable experience. In this study, we propose three novel methods for the effective development of desired derivative models used in Stable Diffusion. The proposed methods facilitate the creation of new image generation models through “merging” process, making it easier to predict the features of the merged model. The proposed methods extend task arithmetic, which enables parameter operations between models, into the merging process. To achieve this, we propose and utilize the “feature score” using CLIP. In this paper, we conducted experiments on the overall parameter operations using feature scores with five models and specific labels. The experimental results showed that the reflection of features based on the task vector's multiply value acquired results with relatively small prediction errors. The potential of the proposed methods was confirmed.

articleTitle: Proposal of a Long - Text Generation Method Considering Article Structure Using ChatGPT
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This study presents an innovative approach for the controlled generation of long Japanese texts using Large Lan-guage Models (LLMs). By incorporating abstracted structural el-ements from article data, we aim to maintain text length, content relevance, and coherence. Our method employs two LLMs: one to extract structural elements and another to generate texts based on these elements. Evaluations against baseline models using the Livedoor news corpus indicate that our approach outperforms in producing controlled-length texts with enhanced vocabulary and expression diversity. LLM-based evaluations and LIME analysis reveal that our method generates more original and content-relevant texts while adhering to the desired structures. However, the effectiveness varies across categories, suggesting the need for refined control mechanisms. This research offers valuable insights into controlled long-text generation in Japanese, with implications for various NLP tasks. Future work will focus on developing more sophisticated control methods and exploring applications in other languages and domains.

articleTitle: Comparative Foot Traffic Analysis During Normal Periods and Firework Events Using Wi-Fi Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Recent observations indicate an increase in the frequency of crowd crush incidents, highlighting the urgent need for effective mitigation strategies. Addressing this issue necessitates a comprehensive understanding of the factors influencing visitor decision-making to prevent adverse outcomes such as crowd crushes. This study introduces a Streamlit dashboard designed to visualize foot traffic data in the Sendagaya area and integrates contextual data from 10 key factors, including events and locations, points of interest (POIs), periods of time, online search activity, height of buildings, temperature and weather conditions, currency exchange rates, earthquakes, number of international flight arrivals, and hotel room rates. This integration facilitates comparative analysis of foot traffic patterns during standard periods versus periods coinciding with significant events, such as the 2023 Jingu Gaien Fireworks Festival, to assess their impact on congestion levels. Conducted exclusively in Sendagaya, the study utilized 8 Wi-Fi sensors throughout August 2023, encompassing 3 key stages: data collection, preprocessing, and dashboard development. The analysis revealed significant determinants-including events, points of interest, time periods, and online activity-that influence visitor foot traffic, while other factors exhibited no discernible impact. These findings have important implications for enhancing decision-making processes, preparedness measures, risk management strategies, and data-driven policymaking for sustainable tourism development.

articleTitle: Prioritizing and Ranking Ships in Multi-encounter Scenarios for Autonomous Navigation*
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This study presents a novel method for prioritizing vessels in multi-encounter scenarios, enhancing autonomous ship collision avoidance control. The method calculates a vessel's priority, i.e. ranking index, by considering factors such as collision risk, give-way responsibilities according to rules, vessel's maneuverability, and surrounding navigable waters. The fuzzy inference method is used to assign scalar values to collision risk, give-way responsibility, and maneuverability terms, while navigable water is evaluated based on the free space around a vessel. The method's applicability is demonstrated through three use cases: 1) Single-time step evaluation, 2) Sequential problem-solving, and 3) Continuous monitoring of priorities. The proposed method offers a range of functionalities applicable to various maritime scenarios, including monitoring and situational awareness, collision avoidance, sequential trajectory planning, and ship-to-ship negotiation.

articleTitle: Learner's Changes in the Number of Solved Problems and Impression of Collaborative Learning with a Robot Using the Problem-Number Negotiation Method
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In recent years, educational-support-robots have attracted considerable attention. In conventional collaborative learning with robots, the number of problems to be answered by the learner (the number of solved problems) is predetermined. This approach precludes learners from engaging in self-directed learning, where they are able to determine the number of solved problems independently. As an alternative, previous studies proposed the Problem-Number Negotiation Method, which involves a dialogue between the learner and the robot prior to the commencement of learning. Previous studies have indicated that short-term collaborative learning with a robot using the Problem-Number Negotiation Method (proposed robot) has the potential to enhance learners' abilities to improve the number of solved problems. However, the previous studies have not verified the changes in the number of solved problems and the impression of the robot in long-term collaborative learning. This paper examines the changes in the number of solved problems and the impression of the robot on university students during long-term collaborative learning. The experimental results found that the proposed robot can spontaneously answer a larger number of solved problems than the conventional robot even during long-term collaborative learning. Moreover, the proposed robot gave the same impressions as the conventional robot.

articleTitle: Preliminary Study on Emotion Analysis of News Comments Based on PAD Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: In this study, we aim to calculate and classify the emotional values of many comments on online news and analyze the emotion trends. In this paper, to calculate the emotional values of comments (Pleasure, Arousal, and Dominance), we first estimate the PAD values of each word contained in the comment using the Japanese version of the ‘Affective Norms for English Words (ANEW) dictionary’ and the similarity of each word in the comment, and then add these up. Furthermore, we obtain news comments and apply the proposed method, and use the results to classify the comments and analyze the emotional trends.

articleTitle: Differentiating Idiopathic Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus Using Multi-Head Attention CNN with Diversify-Loss in Brain MRI
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Idiopathic Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus (iNPH) is characterized by excessive accumulation of cerebrospinal fluid in the cerebral ventricles, leading to symptoms such as gait disturbances, cognitive impairments, and urinary incontinence. Shunt surgery can significantly improve these symptoms. Conversely, Progressive Supranuclear Palsy (PSP) presents similar symptoms but lacks effective treatment options, making accurate differentiation crucial. Traditional methods, which rely on visual assessment of brain MRI, can be challenging without a specialist and are prone to intra- and inter-observer variability. This study proposes an automated approach using a Multi-head Attention Convolutional Neural Network (MA-CNN) with Diversify-Loss to differentiate iNPH from PSP. The proposed method was validated on 39 iNPH and 39 PSP subjects and achieved an accuracy of 0.962 and an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.978, significantly outperforming both the conventional CNN (accuracy of 0.822 and AUC of 0.936) and the method without Diversify-Loss (accuracy of 0.911 and AUC of 0.966). These results indicate that automated differentiation is feasible and that attention maps coupled with Diversify-Loss significantly enhance diagnostic accuracy.

articleTitle: Combined Plant and Control Co-design via Solutions of Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman Equation Based on Physics-informed Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This paper addresses integrated design of engineering systems, where physical structure of the plant and controller design are optimized simultaneously. To cope with uncertainties due to noises acting on the dynamics and modeling errors, an Uncertain Control Co-design (UCCD) problem formulation is proposed. Existing UCCD methods usually rely on uncertainty propagation analyses using Monte CaIro methods for open-loop solutions of optimal control, which suffer from stringent trade-offs among accuracy, time horizon, and computational time. The proposed method utilizes closed-loop solutions characterized by the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation, a Partial Differential Equation (PDE) defined on the state space. A solution algorithm for the proposed UCCD formulation is developed based on PDE solutions of Physics-informed Neural Networks (PINNs). Numerical examples of regulator design problems are provided, and it is shown that simultaneous update of PINN weights and the design parameters effectively works for solving UCCD problems.

articleTitle: DeepFuzzLoc Positioning: A Unified Fusion of Fuzzy Clustering and Deep Learning for Scalable Indoor Localization Using Wi-Fi RSSI
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This research introduces a novel method for indoor positioning by integrating Fuzzy C-Means clustering with deep learning autoencoders, leveraging Wi-Fi RSSI fingerprinting for precise location prediction and building and floor level classification within a unified framework. The approach combines the comprehensibility of Fuzzy C-Means (FCM) with the robust feature extraction capabilities of deep autoencoders through a dual-phase strategy: extensive offline training utilizing RSSI fingerprint data followed by real-time online position prediction. The model's performance was rigorously tested using 5-Fold cross-validation, examining its effectiveness both with and without the integration of FCM on various cluster numbers. Evaluation metrics, including Euclidean distance error for regression and accuracy, F1-score, precision, and specificity for classification effectiveness, were used for comparative analysis. The results were visualized through regression plots, confusion matrices, and learning curves, supplemented by t-SNE visualizations that provide profound insights into the feature space. These detailed analyses highlight the considerable promise of this integrated approach in enhancing the accuracy and reliability of indoor positioning systems.

articleTitle: Sustainable Artificial Intelligence Must Be Aware of Its Body and the Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Awareness computing (AC) has been pursued for decades as an emergent discipline studying the system's ability of observing itself and its environments, and making decisions based on its experiences. Awareness is a subset of intelligent behavior, and as such, it is required but not sufficient to achieve intelligence, including Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Artificial General Intelligence (AGI). Many of today's cutting-edge AI/AGI tools fall short of demonstrating even the most basic properties of awareness, thus they cannot be considered intelligent by any practical measure. Instead of attempting to achieve AI/AGI by scaling-up and recruiting extraordinary amount of data, computational power, and energy, lessons learnt for biological awareness teach us to aim at the efficient use of limited resources as a result of evolutionary pressure. This implies possibly downscaling the system by selecting the essential aspects from the mostly irrelevant data dusts. This work introduces biologically-motivated principles of embodied cognition, to be used in building artificial systems with elements of awareness and intentional action, operating in real time with limited resources.

articleTitle: A Systemic and Semiotic Approach to Thoughts and Meaning Creation Manifested in Intentional Actions
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Intensive research is going on to explore the nature of coherent thought patterns and the creation of meaning that lead to intentional action. This work describes semiosis for symbols and several kinds of meaning, with a focus on semantic and pragmatic meaning. We apply a system's approach to thought and meaning creation, in which mind and brain are complementary parts. We summarize the state-of-art regarding the cycle of creation of knowledge and meaning, using pragmatic information (PI). The main contribution of this work is the introduction of the PI peak-per-second index to characterize coherent thought patterns and meaning creation. Human EEG experiments illustrate the practical benefit of the newly introduced index, when the brain is described as a queueing system that processes thought and meaning.

articleTitle: On Colorectal-Cancer Grading Using Fine-Tuning Based Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Cancer grading is a major challenge for pathologists. In pathological examination, a portion of the cancer (tissue) is taken and observed under a microscope (biopsy) to make a definitive diagnosis. Since the malignancy of cancer is qualitatively evaluated by pathologists' visual inspection, the evaluations deeply depend on skill of pathologists. In other words, the result for some tissue often varies among pathologists. To provide reliable and stable analysis, we propose a method of grading colorectal cancer, using convolutional neural networks (CNNs), In the proposed method, colorectal cancer images are presented to CNNs such as ResNet and DenseNet as data, and fine tuning is adopted. The constructed networks correspond to cancer-grading models, and grade classification experiments are conducted for images of colorectal cancer tissues with three grades using them. It is established, from the classification results, that the AUC exceeds 0.920 in all cases of Grade 1 and Grade 2 images versus Grade 3 images, and Grade 1 images versus Grade 2 and Grade 3 images. In addition, the AUC exceeds 0.880 in the cases of classifying Grade 1 images and Grade 2 images, and those of Grade 2 images and Grade 3 images. The proposed method thus copes well with grading colorectal cancer tissues.

articleTitle: On-Time and Energy-Saving Optimization of Train Auto Driving Based on Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: This paper proposes a reinforcement learning-based approach to optimize train operations for punctuality and energy efficiency. Using the Tokaido Shinkansen line between Shin-Yokohama and Nagoya as a case study, we demonstrate how reinforcement learning can learn optimal speed-time curves that balance these two objectives. Through the construction of a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) reinforcement learning model and computer experiments, the results show that the optimized curve obtained by this method reduces energy consumption by approximately 1.93 % compared to the initially set curve, while meeting punctuality requirements.

articleTitle: Prospect Theory-Based Formulation of Portfolio Optimization Problem using Loan And Its Solution by Evolutionary Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 Joint 13th International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and 25th International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
abstract: Portfolio optimization that allows the borrowed money from a loan to be invested in risk assets is formulated as a data-driven optimization problem called POL_P. Then, in order to reflect investor preferences called “values” in the solution, or the portfolio, prospect theory is used to extend POL_P to another optimization problem called POL_ V. POL_P maximizes the profit of the portfolio, while POL_ V maximizes the value of the portfolio. An evolutionary algorithm with a novel constraint-handling technique is proposed for solving POL_P and POL_ V. Finally, the solutions to POL_P and POL_ V are compared and discussed through experiments using historical asset data.
